title.zh: 卷六十六 志第十七下: 河渠三
title.raw: 卷六十六 志第十七下: 河渠三 Volume 66 Treatises 19: Rivers and Canals 3

sentences.zh: 河渠三 ○黃河

translations.literal: Rivers and Canals 3 ○ The Yellow River
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and Canals 3 — The Yellow River

sentences.zh: 至正四年夏五月，大雨二十餘日，黃河暴溢，水平地深二丈許，北決白茅堤。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer in the fourth year of Zhizheng, heavy rain fell for more than twenty days; the Yellow River burst its banks violently, and the water stood about two zhang deep on level ground, breaking through the Baimao Dike to the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer in Zhizheng 4 (1344), rain fell heavily for over twenty days. The Yellow River surged out of its banks until the flood stood some two zhang deep across the plain, and the river broke north through the Baimao Dike.

sentences.zh: 六月，又北決金堤，並河郡邑濟寧、單州、虞城、碭山、金鄉、魚臺、豐、沛、定陶、楚丘、武城，以至曹州、東明、鉅野、鄆城、嘉祥、汶上、任城等處皆罹水患，民老弱昏墊，壯者流離四方。

translations.literal: In the sixth month it again broke north through the Jindi Dike; along the river, the prefectures and districts of Jining, Shanzhou, Yucheng, Dangshan, Jinxiang, Yutai, Feng, Pei, Dingtao, Qiuqiu, Wucheng, and on to Caozhou, Dongming, Juye, Yuncheng, Jiaxiang, Wenshang, Rencheng, and other places all suffered flood disaster; the old and weak were drowned in confusion, and the strong scattered in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the river broke north again through the Jindi Dike. Every county and town along its course—from Jining, Shanzhou, Yucheng, and Dangshan through Feng, Pei, Dingtao, and beyond to Caozhou, Dongming, Juye, Yuncheng, Jiaxiang, Wenshang, Rencheng, and the rest—was stricken by flood. The elderly and infirm were swept under in the deluge, while able-bodied people fled in every direction.

sentences.zh: 水勢北侵安山，沿入會通、運河，延袤濟南、河間，將壞兩漕司鹽場，妨國計甚重。

translations.literal: The flood pressed north into Anshan, flowed along into the Huitong and transport canals, and spread across Jinan and Hejian; it was about to destroy the salt works of both transport offices, gravely harming the national revenue plan.
translations.idiomatic: The floodwaters drove north into Anshan and poured into the Huitong and Grand Canal, spreading through Jinan and Hejian and threatening to ruin the salt fields of both transport bureaus—a blow of grave consequence to state finances.

sentences.zh: 省臣以聞，朝廷患之，遣使體量，仍督大臣訪求治河方略。

translations.literal: The provincial officials reported it; the court was troubled by it, sent envoys to survey the damage on the ground, and still urged great ministers to seek strategies for controlling the river.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials reported the disaster to court, which was deeply alarmed. It dispatched envoys to survey the damage and ordered senior ministers to search out plans for bringing the river under control.

sentences.zh: 九年冬，脫脫既復為丞相，慨然有志於事功，論及河決，即言於帝，請躬任其事，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the ninth year, after Toghto had again become chancellor, he was stirred with ambition for achievement; when the discussion turned to the river breach, he at once spoke to the emperor, asking to take personal charge of the matter, and the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Zhizheng 9 (1349), Toghto had returned to the chancellorship and was eager to accomplish something lasting. When the breached Yellow River came up for discussion, he asked the emperor to let him take personal charge of the project, and the emperor gladly agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃命集群臣議廷中，而言人人殊，唯都漕運使賈魯，昌言必當治。

translations.literal: He then ordered the gathering of ministers to deliberate in court; each man's words differed, but only the Director of Transport Jia Lu spoke forthrightly that it must be treated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the ministers to debate the matter in court. Opinions diverged widely, but Jia Lu, Director of Transport, alone declared forthrightly that the river had to be brought under control.

sentences.zh: 先是，魯嘗為山東道奉使宣撫首領官，循行被水郡邑，具得修捍成策；

translations.literal: Earlier, Lu had served as chief officer of the Shandong Circuit imperial commissioner for pacification and consolation, touring the flooded prefectures and districts and obtaining in full the established policies for repair and defense;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jia Lu had served as chief officer on the Shandong circuit pacification commission, touring flood-stricken counties and towns and mastering the proven methods of dike repair and flood defense;

sentences.zh: 後又為都水使者，奉旨詣河上相視，驗狀為圖，以二策進獻：一議修築北堤以制橫潰，其用功省；

translations.literal: later he again served as Commissioner of Waterworks, received the imperial order to go to the river to inspect on the spot, verified conditions and made maps, and presented two plans for submission: one proposed building the northern dike to control lateral breach, its labor being economical;
translations.idiomatic: He later became Commissioner of Waterworks and was sent to inspect the river on imperial orders. After surveying conditions and drawing maps, he submitted two plans: one called for strengthening the northern dike to halt lateral breaches, at relatively modest cost;

sentences.zh: 一議疏塞並舉，挽河使東行以復故道，其功費甚大。

translations.literal: one proposed dredging and blocking together, turning the river to flow east and restore the old channel, its labor and expense being very great.
translations.idiomatic: the other proposed dredging and blocking together, forcing the river eastward back into its old course, at vastly greater labor and expense.

sentences.zh: 至是復以二策封，脫脫韙其後策。

translations.literal: At this time he again sealed and submitted the two plans; Toghto approved the latter plan.
translations.idiomatic: Now he again submitted both plans in sealed memorials, and Toghto endorsed the second.

sentences.zh: 議定，乃薦魯於帝，大稱旨。

translations.literal: Once the deliberation was settled, he then recommended Lu to the emperor, who was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once policy was settled, Toghto recommended Jia Lu to the emperor, who was thoroughly pleased.

sentences.zh: 十一年四月初四日，下詔中外，命魯以工部尚書為總治河防使，進秩二品，授以銀印。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the fourth month of the eleventh year, an edict was issued within and without, appointing Lu as Minister of Works and Commissioner General for Yellow River Control, promoting his rank to the second grade and conferring a silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the fourth month of Zhizheng 11 (1351), an edict went out to the empire appointing Jia Lu Minister of Works and Commissioner General for Yellow River Control, raising him to second rank and granting a silver seal.

sentences.zh: 發汴梁、大名十有三路民十五萬人，廬州等戍十有八翼軍二萬人供役，一切從事大小軍民，咸稟節度，便宜興繕。

translations.literal: From the thirteen circuits of Bianliang, Daming, and others, 150,000 civilians were mobilized; from the eighteen wings of garrison troops at Luzhou and elsewhere, 20,000 soldiers were supplied for labor; all civilians and soldiers great and small engaged in the work were subject to his command, with discretionary authority to undertake construction.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred fifty thousand civilians were drafted from the thirteen circuits centered on Bianliang and Daming, and twenty thousand troops from eighteen garrison wings at Luzhou and elsewhere were put to work. Every laborer, soldier or civilian, fell under Jia Lu's command, with full authority to undertake construction as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 是月二十二日鳩工，七月疏鑿成，八月決水故河，九月舟楫通行，十一月水土工畢，諸掃諸堤成。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of that month labor was assembled; in the seventh month dredging and excavation were completed; in the eighth month water was released into the old channel; in the ninth month boats and oars passed freely; in the eleventh month earth and water works were finished, and all fascines and dikes were completed.
translations.idiomatic: Labor was mustered on the twenty-second of that month. Dredging was finished in the seventh month, the sluice was opened into the old channel in the eighth, boats were passing by the ninth, and by the eleventh month all earthworks and waterworks were done—every fascine revetment and every dike in place.

sentences.zh: 河乃復故道，南匯於淮，又東入於海。

translations.literal: The river then returned to its old channel, flowing south to join the Huai, and again east into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River returned to its old course, flowing south to join the Huai and then eastward to the sea.

sentences.zh: 帝遣貴臣報祭河伯，召魯還京師，論功超拜榮祿大夫、集賢大學士，其宣力諸臣遷賞有差，賜丞相脫脫世襲答剌罕之號，特命翰林學士承旨歐陽玄制河平碑文，以旌勞績。

translations.literal: The emperor sent eminent officials to report the sacrifice to the River Lord, summoned Lu back to the capital, and for merit promoted him beyond regular rank to Grand Master for Glorious Emolument and Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies; the various ministers who had exerted themselves were promoted and rewarded in differing degrees; the chancellor Toghto was granted the hereditary title of Darqan; and the Hanlin Academician Ouyang Xuan was specially ordered to compose the Stele on Pacifying the River, to honor the labor and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent high officials to report the sacrifice to the River Lord and summoned Jia Lu back to the capital. For his service Jia Lu was promoted beyond the usual grades to Grand Master for Glorious Emolument and Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies; other officials who had labored on the project received promotions and rewards in varying measure; Chancellor Toghto was granted the hereditary title of Darqan; and Hanlin Academician Ouyang Xuan was commissioned to compose the Stele on Pacifying the River, to commemorate the achievement.

sentences.zh: 玄既為河平之碑，又自以為司馬遷、班固記河渠溝洫，僅載治水之道，不言其方，使後世任斯事者無所考則，乃從魯訪問方略，及詢過客，質吏牘，作《至正河防記》，欲使來世罹河患者按而求之。

translations.literal: After Xuan had composed the stele on pacifying the river, he also considered that Sima Qian and Ban Gu in recording rivers and canals and irrigation ditches had only set down the principles of controlling water, not their methods, so that later generations charged with such tasks had nothing by which to examine and follow; he therefore sought plans and methods from Lu, also questioned passing travelers, verified against official documents, and wrote the Record of Zhizheng River Control, wishing that future generations afflicted by the river might seek and find guidance in it.
translations.idiomatic: After composing the pacification stele, Ouyang Xuan reflected that Sima Qian and Ban Gu, in their treatises on rivers and canals, recorded only general principles of water control, not the practical methods—leaving later engineers nothing concrete to follow. He therefore interviewed Jia Lu about his methods, questioned travelers who had witnessed the work, checked official records, and wrote the Record of Zhizheng River Control so that future generations facing river disasters might find actionable guidance within it.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：

translations.literal: Its words say:
translations.idiomatic: It reads in part:

sentences.zh: 治河一也，有疏、有浚、有塞，三者異焉。

translations.literal: Controlling the river is one task, yet there are channeling, dredging, and blocking—the three differ.
translations.idiomatic: River control is a single enterprise, but it comprises three distinct methods: channeling, dredging, and blocking.

sentences.zh: 釃河之流，因而導之，謂之疏。

translations.literal: To strain the river's flow and thereby guide it is called channeling.
translations.idiomatic: To divide the river's current and guide it along a chosen path is called channeling (shu).

sentences.zh: 去河之淤，因而深之，謂之浚。

translations.literal: To remove the river's silt and thereby deepen it is called dredging.
translations.idiomatic: To remove sediment from the riverbed and thereby deepen the channel is called dredging (jun).

sentences.zh: 抑河之暴，因而扼之，謂之塞。

translations.literal: To restrain the river's violence and thereby choke it is called blocking.
translations.idiomatic: To restrain the river's fury and choke off its escape is called blocking (sai).

sentences.zh: 疏浚之別有四：曰生地，曰故道，曰河身，曰減水河。

translations.literal: The subdivisions of channeling and dredging are four: called new ground, old channel, river body, and flood-relief channel.
translations.idiomatic: Channeling and dredging fall into four categories: work through new ground, work in the old channel, work on the river body itself, and work on flood-relief channels.

sentences.zh: 生地有直有紆，因直而鑿之，可就故道。

translations.literal: New ground may be straight or winding; by cutting along the straight course one can reach the old channel.
translations.idiomatic: New ground may run straight or wind about; cutting along the straighter line can bring the channel back to the old course.

sentences.zh: 故道有高有卑，高者平之以趨卑，高卑相就，則高不壅，卑不瀦，慮夫壅生潰，瀦生堙也。

translations.literal: The old channel has high and low sections; the high are leveled to approach the low; when high and low meet, then the high does not dam up and the low does not pond, for fear that damming produces breach and ponding produces silting.
translations.idiomatic: The old channel has high and low stretches: the highs must be leveled down toward the lows so that water does not dam up on the highs or pool on the lows—for a dammed stretch breeds breaches, and a pooled stretch breeds siltation.

sentences.zh: 河身者，水雖通行，身有廣狹，狹難受水，水益悍，故狹者以計辟之；

translations.literal: As for the river body, though water may pass, the body has wide and narrow parts; narrow parts have difficulty receiving water and the water grows fiercer, so narrow parts are widened by planned cutting;
translations.idiomatic: The river body may carry water, yet its width varies: narrow stretches cannot take the full flow and the current grows violent, so narrow sections must be deliberately widened;

sentences.zh: 廣難為岸，岸善崩，故廣者以計禦之。

translations.literal: wide parts have difficulty forming banks, and banks readily collapse, so wide parts are defended by planned measures.
translations.idiomatic: wide stretches are hard to bank and banks there collapse easily, so wide sections must be deliberately fortified.

sentences.zh: 減水河者，水放曠則以制其狂，水隳突則以殺其怒。

translations.literal: As for flood-relief channels, when water runs wild they are used to control its frenzy; when water smashes and rushes they are used to quell its rage.
translations.idiomatic: Flood-relief channels tame the river when it runs unrestrained, and bleed off its force when it surges destructively.

sentences.zh: 治堤一也，有創築、修築、補築之名，有剌水堤，有截河堤，有護岸堤，有縷水堤，有石船堤。

translations.literal: Dike work is also one task, with the designations of new construction, repair construction, and patch construction; there are spike-water dikes, river-cutting dikes, bank-protecting dikes, thread-water dikes, and stone-ship dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Dike work is likewise a single category, subdivided into new construction, repair, and patching. It includes spike-water dikes, river-cutting dikes, bank-protecting dikes, thread-water dikes, and stone-ship dikes.

sentences.zh: 治掃一也，有岸掃、水掃，有龍尾、欄頭、馬頭等掃。

translations.literal: Fascine work is also one task; there are bank fascines and water fascines, and fascines such as dragon-tail, railing-head, and horse-head types.
translations.idiomatic: Fascine revetment is another unified category, comprising bank fascines and water fascines, with types named dragon-tail, railing-head, horse-head, and the like.

sentences.zh: 其為掃臺及推卷、牽制、珣掛之法，有用土、用石、用鐵、用草、用木、用杙、用縆之方。

translations.literal: The methods for building fascine platforms and rolling, restraining, and suspending fascines employ earth, stone, iron, grass, wood, stakes, and ropes in their techniques.
translations.idiomatic: Building fascine platforms and the techniques of rolling, anchoring, and suspending fascines draw on earth, stone, iron, grass, timber, stakes, and rope in various combinations.

sentences.zh: 塞河一也，有缺口，有豁口，有龍口。

translations.literal: Blocking the river is also one task; there are breach gaps, notch gaps, and dragon mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Blocking the river is likewise one enterprise, with breach gaps, notch gaps, and dragon mouths.

sentences.zh: 缺口者，已成川。

translations.literal: A breach gap is one that has already become a channel.
translations.idiomatic: A breach gap is a break that has already become a full channel.

sentences.zh: 豁口者，舊常為水所豁，水退則口下於堤，水漲則溢出於口。

translations.literal: A notch gap is one that water has long scoured open; when water recedes the opening lies below the dike, and when water rises it overflows through the opening.
translations.idiomatic: A notch gap is a place the river has long scoured open: when the water falls the opening sits below the dike crest, and when it rises the flood spills through the notch.

sentences.zh: 龍口者，水之所會，自新河入故道之潀也。

translations.literal: A dragon mouth is where waters converge, the rush from the new channel into the old channel.
translations.idiomatic: A dragon mouth is the confluence where the new channel pours into the old—the critical junction of the whole project.

sentences.zh: 此外不能悉書，因其用功之次第，而就述於其下焉。

translations.literal: Beyond this not everything can be written in full; following the sequence of labor applied, the account is set forth below.
translations.idiomatic: Not every detail can be recorded here; what follows is arranged in the order the work was actually carried out.

sentences.zh: 其浚故道，深廣不等，通長二百八十里百五十四步而強。

translations.literal: The dredging of the old channel, with depth and width unequal, totaled in length two hundred eighty li, one hundred fifty-four paces, and a fraction more.
translations.idiomatic: Dredging the old channel—depth and width varying along its course—ran in all to two hundred eighty li, one hundred fifty-four paces, and a fraction.

sentences.zh: 功始自白茅，長百八十二里。

translations.literal: The work began from Baimao, a length of one hundred eighty-two li.
translations.idiomatic: Work began at Baimao and extended one hundred eighty-two li.

sentences.zh: 繼自黃陵岡至南白茅，辟生地十里。

translations.literal: Continuing from Huangling Hillock to South Baimao, new ground was opened for ten li.
translations.idiomatic: From Huangling Hillock to South Baimao a new channel ten li long was cut through undeveloped ground.

sentences.zh: 口初受，廣百八十步，深二丈有二尺，已下停廣百步，高下不等，相折深二丈及泉。

translations.literal: At the mouth where it first received water, the width was one hundred eighty paces and the depth two zhang and two chi; below that the even width was one hundred paces, with height and depth unequal, adjusted in stages to a depth of two zhang down to the spring level.
translations.idiomatic: At the intake mouth the channel was one hundred eighty paces wide and two zhang two chi deep; downstream it was leveled to an even width of one hundred paces, with depth adjusted in stages to two zhang down to spring level.

sentences.zh: 曰停、曰折者，用古算法，因此推彼，知其勢之低昂，相準折而取勻停也。

translations.literal: What is called 'even' and 'adjusted' employs the ancient computational method, inferring one point from another to know the rise and fall of the terrain, matching stages to obtain uniform evenness.
translations.idiomatic: The terms 'even' (ting) and 'adjusted' (zhe) refer to an ancient surveying method: measuring one section to infer the next, gauging how the terrain rises and falls, and grading the channel in stages until the slope was uniform.

sentences.zh: 南白茅至劉莊村，接入故道十里，通折墾廣八十步，深九尺。

translations.literal: From South Baimao to Liuzhuang Village, joining the old channel for ten li, the adjusted dredged width was eighty paces and the depth nine chi.
translations.idiomatic: From South Baimao to Liuzhuang Village the work joined the old channel for ten li, dredged to an adjusted width of eighty paces and depth of nine chi.

sentences.zh: 劉莊至專固，百有二里二百八十步，通折停廣六十步，深五尺。

translations.literal: From Liuzhuang to Zhuangu, one hundred two li and two hundred eighty paces, the adjusted even width was sixty paces and the depth five chi.
translations.idiomatic: From Liuzhuang to Zhuangu—one hundred two li and two hundred eighty paces—the channel was graded to an even width of sixty paces and depth of five chi.

sentences.zh: 專固至黃固，墾生地八里，面廣百步，底廣九十步，高下相折，深丈有五尺。

translations.literal: From Zhuangu to Huanggu, dredging new ground for eight li, the surface width was one hundred paces, the bottom width ninety paces, with height adjusted in stages, and the depth one zhang and five chi.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhuangu to Huanggu workers cut eight li through new ground, with a surface width of one hundred paces, bottom width of ninety paces, graded slope, and depth of one zhang five chi.

sentences.zh: 黃固至哈只口，長五十一里八十步，相折停廣墾六十步，深五尺。

translations.literal: From Huanggu to Hazhi Mouth, a length of fifty-one li and eighty paces, with adjusted even dredged width of sixty paces and depth five chi.
translations.idiomatic: From Huanggu to Hazhi Mouth—fifty-one li and eighty paces—the dredged width was graded to sixty paces even and depth to five chi.

sentences.zh: 乃浚凹裏減水河，通長九十八里百五十四步。

translations.literal: Then the Aoli flood-relief channel was dredged, totaling in length ninety-eight li and one hundred fifty-four paces.
translations.idiomatic: Workers next dredged the Aoli flood-relief channel, ninety-eight li and one hundred fifty-four paces in all.

sentences.zh: 凹裏村缺河口生地，長三里四十步，面廣六十步，底廣四十步，深一丈四尺。

translations.literal: At Aoli Village breach-gap mouth new ground, a length of three li and forty paces, surface width sixty paces, bottom width forty paces, depth one zhang and four chi.
translations.idiomatic: At the breach-gap mouth near Aoli Village, new ground three li and forty paces long was cut with a surface width of sixty paces, bottom width of forty paces, and depth of one zhang four chi.

sentences.zh: 自凹裏生地以下舊河身至張贊店，長八十二里五十四步。

translations.literal: From Aoli new ground downstream through the old river body to Zhangzan Shop, a length of eighty-two li and fifty-four paces.
translations.idiomatic: From the Aoli new ground downstream through the old riverbed to Zhangzan Shop measured eighty-two li and fifty-four paces.

sentences.zh: 上三十六里，墾廣二十步，深五尺；

translations.literal: The upper thirty-six li, dredged width twenty paces, depth five chi;
translations.idiomatic: The upper thirty-six li were dredged twenty paces wide and five chi deep;

sentences.zh: 中三十五里，墾廣二十八步，深五尺；

translations.literal: the middle thirty-five li, dredged width twenty-eight paces, depth five chi;
translations.idiomatic: the middle thirty-five li twenty-eight paces wide and five chi deep;

sentences.zh: 下十里二百四十步，墾廣二十六步，深五尺。

translations.literal: the lower ten li and two hundred forty paces, dredged width twenty-six paces, depth five chi.
translations.idiomatic: the lower ten li and two hundred forty paces twenty-six paces wide and five chi deep.

sentences.zh: 張贊店至楊青村，接入故道，墾生地十有三里六十步，面廣六十步，底廣四十步，深一丈四尺。

translations.literal: From Zhangzan Shop to Yangqing Village, joining the old channel, dredging new ground for thirteen li and sixty paces, surface width sixty paces, bottom width forty paces, depth one zhang and four chi.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhangzan Shop to Yangqing Village the channel rejoined the old course after thirteen li and sixty paces of new ground dredged to a surface width of sixty paces, bottom width of forty paces, and depth of one zhang four chi.

sentences.zh: 其塞專固缺口，修堤三重，並補築凹裏減水河南岸豁口，通長二十里三百十有七步。

translations.literal: The blocking of the Zhuangu breach gap, with repair of three tiers of dikes, and patching of the notch gaps on the south bank of the Aoli flood-relief channel, totaled in length twenty li and three hundred seventeen paces.
translations.idiomatic: Blocking the Zhuangu breach gap involved three tiers of dikes plus patching notch gaps on the south bank of the Aoli flood-relief channel—twenty li and three hundred seventeen paces in all.

sentences.zh: 其創築河口前第一重西堤，南北長三百三十步，面廣二十五步，底廣三十三步，樹置樁橛，實以土牛、草葦、雜梢相兼，高丈有三尺，堤前置龍尾大掃。

translations.literal: The newly built first-tier western dike before the river mouth, three hundred thirty paces long north to south, surface width twenty-five paces, bottom width thirty-three paces, with piles and stakes set, filled with a mixture of earth clods, reeds, and assorted brush, height one zhang and three chi, with a great dragon-tail fascine placed before the dike.
translations.idiomatic: The first new western dike before the river mouth ran three hundred thirty paces north to south, twenty-five paces wide at the crest and thirty-three at the base, reinforced with piles and packed with earth clods, reeds, and brush to a height of one zhang three chi, with a great dragon-tail fascine set before it.

sentences.zh: 言龍尾者，伐大樹連梢系之堤旁，隨水上下，以破嚙岸浪者也。

translations.literal: What is called 'dragon-tail' means felling large trees with branches attached and tying them beside the dike, moving up and down with the water, to break the waves that gnaw the bank.
translations.idiomatic: A 'dragon-tail' fascine consists of large trees felled with branches still attached, moored beside the dike to ride the water up and down and break the waves that chew at the bank.

sentences.zh: 築第二重正堤，並補兩端舊堤，通長十有一里三百步。

translations.literal: The second-tier main dike was built, and the old dikes at both ends were patched, totaling in length eleven li and three hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: Workers built the second-tier main dike and patched the old dikes at both ends—eleven li and three hundred paces altogether.

sentences.zh: 缺口正堤長四里，兩堤相接舊堤，置樁堵閉河身，長百四十五步，用土牛、草葦、梢土相兼修築，底廣三十步，修高二丈。

translations.literal: The breach-gap main dike was four li long; the two dikes joined the old dike, with piles set to block and close the river body, one hundred forty-five paces long, repaired with a mixture of earth clods, reeds, and brush earth, bottom width thirty paces, repaired height two zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The main dike at the breach gap ran four li, linking to the old dikes on either side. Piles were driven to seal the river channel for one hundred forty-five paces, packed with earth clods, reeds, and brush to a base thirty paces wide and height of two zhang.

sentences.zh: 其岸上土工修築者，長三里二百十有五步有奇，高廣不等，通高一丈五尺。

translations.literal: The earthwork repaired on the bank was three li, two hundred fifteen paces, and a fraction more in length, with height and width unequal, totaling one zhang and five chi in height.
translations.idiomatic: Bank earthworks extended three li, two hundred fifteen paces and a fraction, varying in height and width but averaging one zhang five chi high.

sentences.zh: 補築舊堤者，長七里三百步，表裏倍薄七步，增卑六尺，計高一丈。

translations.literal: The patched old dike was seven li and three hundred paces long; on both faces it was doubled in thinness by seven paces, the low parts raised six chi, totaling one zhang in height.
translations.idiomatic: Patched sections of the old dike ran seven li and three hundred paces; both faces were widened by seven paces, low sections raised six chi, for a total height of one zhang.

sentences.zh: 築第三重東後堤，並接修舊堤，高廣不等，通長八里。

translations.literal: The third-tier eastern rear dike was built, with connected repair of the old dike, height and width unequal, totaling eight li in length.
translations.idiomatic: The third-tier eastern rear dike was built and tied into repaired old dikes—eight li in all, with varying height and width.

sentences.zh: 補築凹裏減水河南岸豁口四處，置樁木，草土相兼，長四十七步。

translations.literal: Four notch gaps on the south bank of the Aoli flood-relief channel were patched, with piles and timber set, grass and earth combined, forty-seven paces in length.
translations.idiomatic: Four notch gaps on the south bank of the Aoli flood-relief channel were patched with piles, timber, grass, and earth—forty-seven paces in all.

sentences.zh: 於是塞黃陵全河，水中及岸上修堤長三十六里百三十六步。

translations.literal: Thereupon the entire river at Huangling was blocked; dikes repaired in the water and on the bank totaled thirty-six li and one hundred thirty-six paces in length.
translations.idiomatic: The full river course at Huangling was then sealed, with dikes built in the water and on the banks totaling thirty-six li and one hundred thirty-six paces.

sentences.zh: 其修大堤刺水者二，長十有四里七十步。

translations.literal: Two great spike-water dikes were repaired, fourteen li and seventy paces in length.
translations.idiomatic: Two great spike-water dikes were built, fourteen li and seventy paces long.

sentences.zh: 其西復作大堤刺水者一，長十有二里百三十步。

translations.literal: To the west another great spike-water dike was made, twelve li and one hundred thirty paces in length.
translations.idiomatic: To the west a third great spike-water dike was added, twelve li and one hundred thirty paces long.

sentences.zh: 內創築岸上土堤，西北起李八宅西堤，東南至舊河岸，長十里百五十步，顛廣四步，趾廣三之，高丈有五尺。

translations.literal: Within this, a bank earth dike was newly built on land, from the northwest starting at the Libazhai western dike, southeast to the old river bank, ten li and one hundred fifty paces long, crest width four paces, toe width three times that, height one zhang and five chi.
translations.idiomatic: A new bank dike was built inland from the Libazhai western dike southeast to the old riverbank—ten li and one hundred fifty paces long, four paces wide at the crest, three times that at the toe, and one zhang five chi high.

sentences.zh: 仍築舊河岸至入水堤，長四百三十步，趾廣三十步，顛殺其六之一，接修入水。

translations.literal: The old river bank was still built out to the in-water dike, four hundred thirty paces long, toe width thirty paces, the crest reduced by one-sixth, connecting in repair into the water.
translations.idiomatic: The old riverbank was extended to the in-water dike for four hundred thirty paces, thirty paces wide at the toe, the crest tapered by one-sixth, and the structure carried down into the water.

sentences.zh: 兩岸掃堤並行。

translations.literal: Fascine dikes on both banks proceeded in parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Fascine revetments were built on both banks simultaneously.

sentences.zh: 作西掃者夏人水工，征自靈武；

translations.literal: Those who made the western fascines were Tangut water workers, conscripted from Lingwu;
translations.idiomatic: The western fascines were built by Tangut water engineers drafted from Lingwu;

sentences.zh: 作東掃者漢人水工，征自近畿。

translations.literal: those who made the eastern fascines were Han water workers, conscripted from the metropolitan vicinity.
translations.idiomatic: the eastern fascines by Han water engineers drafted from the capital region.

sentences.zh: 其法以竹絡實以小石，每掃不等，以蒲葦綿腰索徑寸許者從鋪，廣可一二十步，長可二三十步。

translations.literal: The method used bamboo cages filled with small stones; each fascine was unequal in size; rush-and-reed waist ropes about an inch in diameter were laid along in spreading; the width could be ten or twenty paces, the length twenty or thirty paces.
translations.idiomatic: The method used bamboo cages packed with small stones. Each fascine varied in size. Rush-and-reed waist ropes about an inch thick were laid lengthwise; a fascine might span ten to twenty paces in width and twenty to thirty in length.

sentences.zh: 又以曳掃索徑三寸或四寸、長二百餘尺者衡鋪之。

translations.literal: Drag-fascine ropes three or four inches in diameter and more than two hundred chi long were also laid crosswise.
translations.idiomatic: Drag ropes three or four inches thick and over two hundred chi long were laid across them.

sentences.zh: 相間復以竹葦麻釭大繂，長三百尺者為管心索，就系綿腰索之端於其上，以草數千束，多至萬餘，勻布厚鋪於綿腰索之上，袴而納之，丁夫數千，以足蹈實，推卷稍高，即以水工二人立其上，而號於眾，眾聲力舉，用小大推梯，推卷成掃，高下長短不等，大者高二丈，小者不下丈餘。

translations.literal: At intervals bamboo, reed, hemp, and great cables three hundred chi long were used as core ropes; the ends of the rush waist ropes were tied to them; thousands of bundles of grass, in some cases more than ten thousand, were spread evenly and laid thick atop the waist ropes, tucked and packed in; thousands of laborers trampled them firm with their feet; as rolling raised them slightly, two water workers stood atop and called out to the crowd; with united voices and strength they used large and small pushing ladders to roll the fascine into shape; height and length were unequal—the large ones two zhang high, the small ones no less than one zhang and more.
translations.idiomatic: Between the layers workers laid great cables of bamboo, reed, and hemp three hundred chi long as core ropes, tying the rush waist ropes to them. Thousands of grass bundles—sometimes more than ten thousand—were spread thick and even across the waist ropes, then folded and packed in. Thousands of laborers stamped them firm with their feet. As each roll grew higher, two water engineers stood atop and called the rhythm; the crowd answered in unison and drove the fascine forward with pushing ladders large and small until it took shape. Finished fascines varied in height and length—the largest standing two zhang high, the smallest still over one zhang.

sentences.zh: 又用大索或互為腰索，轉致河濱，選健丁操管心索，順掃臺立踏，或掛之臺中鐵貓大橛之上，以漸縋之下水。

translations.literal: Great ropes were again used, or alternately as waist ropes, and conveyed to the riverbank; sturdy men were chosen to handle the core ropes, standing and treading along the fascine platform, or hanging them on the iron anchors and great stakes in the platform, gradually lowering them into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy ropes served as waist lines to haul the fascines to the riverbank. Strong laborers manned the core ropes, walking the fascine platform or hitching the load to iron anchors and great stakes set in the platform, then lowering it gradually into the water.

sentences.zh: 掃後掘地為渠，陷管心索渠中，以散草厚覆，築之以土，其上復以土牛、雜草、小掃梢土，多寡厚薄，先後隨宜。

translations.literal: After the fascine was placed, a trench was dug in the ground, the core rope sunk in the trench, loose grass spread thickly over it, and earth piled on; above that earth clods, mixed grass, small fascine brush, and earth were again applied, more or less, thick or thin, in sequence as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: After placing a fascine, workers dug a trench, laid the core rope in it, covered it thickly with loose grass, and piled earth on top, then added earth clods, mixed vegetation, small fascine brush, and more earth—amount and thickness adjusted as needed.

sentences.zh: 修疊為掃臺，務使牽制上下，縝密堅壯，互為掎角，掃不動搖。

translations.literal: Layers were built up into a fascine platform, striving to restrain it above and below, tightly dense and solid, mutually bracing like corner supports, so the fascine would not shift or shake.
translations.idiomatic: They built this up into a fascine platform, anchoring it above and below until it was dense, solid, and mutually braced like corner supports so the fascine would not shift.

sentences.zh: 日力不足，火以繼之。

translations.literal: When daylight was insufficient, firelight continued the work.
translations.idiomatic: When daylight failed, they worked by torchlight.

sentences.zh: 積累既畢，復施前法，卷掃以壓先下之掃，量水淺深，制掃厚薄，疊之多至四掃而止。

translations.literal: Once accumulation was complete, the former method was applied again, rolling fascines to press those already placed below, gauging the water's depth and shallow points, controlling fascine thickness, stacking up to four fascines and no more.
translations.idiomatic: When one layer was complete they repeated the process, rolling new fascines to weight those already in the water, adjusting thickness to the depth, and stacking as many as four layers.

sentences.zh: 兩掃之間置竹絡，高二丈或三丈，圍四丈五尺，實以小石、土牛。

translations.literal: Between two fascines bamboo cages were placed, two or three zhang high, four zhang and five chi in girth, filled with small stones and earth clods.
translations.idiomatic: Between fascine layers they set bamboo cages two or three zhang high and four zhang five chi around, packed with small stones and earth clods.

sentences.zh: 既滿，系以竹纜，其兩旁並掃，密下大樁，就以竹絡上大竹腰索系於樁上。

translations.literal: Once filled, they were bound with bamboo cables; on both sides alongside the fascines, great stakes were set densely, and the great bamboo waist ropes atop the bamboo cages were tied to the stakes.
translations.idiomatic: Once filled, the cages were lashed with bamboo cables. Great stakes were driven densely on both sides beside the fascines, and the large bamboo waist ropes atop the cages were tied to them.

sentences.zh: 東西兩掃及其中竹絡之上，以草土等物築為掃臺，約長五十步或百步，再下掃，即以竹索或麻索長八百尺或五百尺者一二，雜廁其餘管心索之間，俟掃入水之後，其餘管心索如前珣掛，隨以管心長索，遠置五七十步之外，或鐵貓，或大樁，曳而系之，通管束累日所下之掃，再以草土等物通修成堤，又以龍尾大掃密掛於護堤大樁，分析水勢。

translations.literal: Upon the eastern and western fascines and the bamboo cages between them, grass, earth, and other materials were built into a fascine platform, about fifty or one hundred paces long; when another fascine was placed below, one or two bamboo or hemp ropes eight hundred or five hundred chi long were interwoven among the remaining core ropes; after the fascine entered the water, the remaining core ropes were suspended as before; then with the long core ropes, set far off fifty or seventy paces away on iron anchors or great stakes, they were hauled and tied, binding together all the fascines placed over successive days; then with grass, earth, and other materials a dike was built through in repair; and great dragon-tail fascines were densely hung on the great stakes protecting the dike to divide the water's force.
translations.idiomatic: On the eastern and western fascines and the cages between them, workers built a platform of grass and earth some fifty or one hundred paces long. Before lowering the next fascine they wove one or two bamboo or hemp ropes five hundred to eight hundred chi long among the remaining core lines. After the fascine sank, the spare core ropes were suspended as before; long core lines were run fifty or seventy paces back to iron anchors or great stakes, hauled taut, and used to bind together all fascines placed over successive days. Grass and earth were then built up into a continuous dike, and great dragon-tail fascines were hung densely from the protective stakes to break the current.

sentences.zh: 其堤長二百七十步，北廣四十二步，中廣五十五步，南廣四十二步，自顛至趾，通高三丈八尺。

translations.literal: This dike was two hundred seventy paces long; the north face forty-two paces wide, the middle fifty-five paces wide, the south forty-two paces wide; from crest to toe the total height was three zhang and eight chi.
translations.idiomatic: This dike ran two hundred seventy paces long—forty-two paces wide on the north face, fifty-five in the middle, forty-two on the south—and stood three zhang eight chi from crest to toe.

sentences.zh: 其截河大堤，高廣不等，長十有九里百七十七步。

translations.literal: The great river-cutting dike, with height and width unequal, was nineteen li and one hundred seventy-seven paces in length.
translations.idiomatic: The great river-cutting dike, varying in height and width, extended nineteen li and one hundred seventy-seven paces.

sentences.zh: 其在黃陵北岸者，長十里四十一步。

translations.literal: That on the north bank at Huangling was ten li and forty-one paces long.
translations.idiomatic: The section on the north bank at Huangling ran ten li and forty-one paces.

sentences.zh: 築岸上土堤，西北起東西故堤，東南至河口，長七里九十七步，顛廣六步，趾倍之而強二步，高丈有五尺，接修入水。

translations.literal: A bank earth dike was built on land, from the northwest starting at the east-west old dike, southeast to the river mouth, seven li and ninety-seven paces long, crest width six paces, toe twice that plus two paces more, height one zhang and five chi, connected in repair into the water.
translations.idiomatic: A bank dike was built from the old east-west dike northwest to the river mouth southeast—seven li and ninety-seven paces long, six paces wide at the crest, twice that plus two at the toe, one zhang five chi high, and carried down into the water.

sentences.zh: 施土牛、小掃梢草雜土，多寡厚薄隨宜修疊，及下竹絡，安大樁，系龍尾掃，如前兩堤法。

translations.literal: Earth clods, small fascine brush, grass, and mixed earth were applied, more or less and thick or thin as appropriate in layered repair; bamboo cages were set down, great stakes installed, and dragon-tail fascines tied, by the same method as the previous two dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Earth clods, small fascines, grass, and mixed earth were layered as needed; bamboo cages were set, great stakes driven, and dragon-tail fascines tied off—by the same method used on the earlier dikes.

sentences.zh: 唯修疊掃臺，增用白闌小石。

translations.literal: Only in building up the fascine platform was additional use made of white fence small stones.
translations.idiomatic: Only in building the fascine platform were additional white limestone pebbles used.

sentences.zh: 並掃上及前幾修掃堤一，長百餘步，直抵龍口。

translations.literal: Parallel fascines above and the fascine dike repaired earlier, one section more than one hundred paces long, ran straight to the dragon mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Parallel fascines above and the earlier fascine dike extended more than one hundred paces straight to the dragon mouth.

sentences.zh: 稍北，欄頭三掃並行，掃大堤廣與刺水二堤不同，通前列四掃，間以竹絡，成一大堤，長二百八十步，北廣百一十步，其顛至水面高丈有五尺，水面至澤腹高二丈五尺，通高三丈五尺；

translations.literal: Slightly to the north, three railing-head fascines proceeded in parallel; the great fascine dike's width differed from the two spike-water dikes; in all four fascines were placed in front, with bamboo cages between them, forming one great dike two hundred eighty paces long; the north face one hundred ten paces wide; from crest to water surface one zhang and five chi high; from water surface to the belly of the marsh two zhang and five chi; total height three zhang and five chi;
translations.idiomatic: Farther north, three railing-head fascines were laid in parallel. The great fascine dike was wider than the two spike-water dikes. Four fascines were set in a row with bamboo cages between, forming one great structure two hundred eighty paces long and one hundred ten paces wide on the north face—one zhang five chi from crest to waterline, two zhang five chi from waterline to the marsh bottom, three zhang five chi in all;

sentences.zh: 中流廣八十步，其顛至水面高丈有五尺，水面至澤腹高五丈五尺，通高七丈。

translations.literal: the midstream section eighty paces wide; from crest to water surface one zhang and five chi high; from water surface to the belly of the marsh five zhang and five chi; total height seven zhang.
translations.idiomatic: the midstream section eighty paces wide stood one zhang five chi above the water, five zhang five chi from waterline to marsh bottom—seven zhang in total height.

sentences.zh: 並創築縷水橫堤一，東起北截河大堤，西抵西刺水大堤。

translations.literal: A thread-water transverse dike was also newly built, starting in the east from the northern river-cutting great dike and reaching in the west to the western spike-water great dike.
translations.idiomatic: A thread-water transverse dike was also built, running east from the northern river-cutting dike to the western spike-water dike.

sentences.zh: 又一堤東起中刺水大堤，西抵西刺水大堤，通長二里四十二步，亦顛廣四步，趾三之，高丈有二尺。

translations.literal: Another dike started in the east from the central spike-water great dike and reached in the west to the western spike-water great dike, totaling two li and forty-two paces in length; its crest was also four paces wide, the toe three times that, and the height one zhang and two chi.
translations.idiomatic: Another dike ran from the central spike-water dike east to the western spike-water dike west—two li and forty-two paces long, four paces wide at the crest, three times that at the toe, and one zhang two chi high.

sentences.zh: 修黃陵南岸，長九里百六十步，內創岸土堤，東北起新補白茅故堤，西南至舊河口，高廣不等，長八里二百五十步。

translations.literal: The south bank at Huangling was repaired, nine li and one hundred sixty paces in length; within this a bank earth dike was newly built, starting in the northeast from the newly patched Baimao old dike, southwest to the old river mouth, with height and width unequal, eight li and two hundred fifty paces long.
translations.idiomatic: The south bank at Huangling was repaired for nine li and one hundred sixty paces. A new bank dike was built northeast from the patched Baimao old dike southwest to the old river mouth—eight li and two hundred fifty paces long, with varying height and width.

sentences.zh: 乃入水作石船大堤，蓋由是秋八月二十九日乙巳道故河流，先所修北岸西中刺水及截河三堤猶短，約水尚少，力未足恃。

translations.literal: Then a stone-ship great dike was built in the water, for on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month of autumn, the day yisi, the old river channel was opened; the three dikes previously built on the north bank—the western, central spike-water, and river-cutting dikes—were still short, holding back only a modest amount of water, and their strength could not yet be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Workers then built a stone-ship dike in the water, because on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month—the day yisi—the old channel was opened. The three dikes already built on the north bank were still too low to hold back much water, and could not yet be trusted to stand.

sentences.zh: 決河勢大，南北廣四百餘步，中流深三丈餘，益以秋漲，水多故河十之八。

translations.literal: The breach river's force was great, more than four hundred paces wide north to south, more than three zhang deep in midstream; added to this was the autumn flood swell, and eight-tenths of the water was in the old channel.
translations.idiomatic: The breach current was immense—over four hundred paces wide and more than three zhang deep at midstream. With the autumn flood swell, eight-tenths of the flow still ran through the old channel.

sentences.zh: 兩河爭流，近故河口，水刷岸北行，洄漩湍激，難以下掃。

translations.literal: The two rivers contended in flow; near the old river mouth the water scoured the bank running north, swirling in eddies and rushing violently, making it difficult to lower fascines.
translations.idiomatic: The two currents fought for the channel. Near the old river mouth the water scoured north along the bank in violent eddies, making it nearly impossible to lower fascines.

sentences.zh: 且掃行或遲，恐水盡湧入決河，因淤故河，前功遂隳。

translations.literal: Moreover, if fascine placement was delayed, there was fear that all the water would surge into the breach river, silting up the old channel, and the previous work would then be ruined.
translations.idiomatic: If fascine work lagged, the entire flow might pour into the breach and silt up the old channel, undoing everything accomplished so far.

sentences.zh: 魯乃精思障水入故河之方，以九月七日癸丑，逆流排大船二十七艘，前後連以大桅或長樁，用大麻索、竹縆絞縛，綴為方舟。

translations.literal: Lu then thought deeply on methods to block water and direct it into the old channel; on the seventh day of the ninth month, the day guichou, twenty-seven large boats were arrayed against the current, linked fore and aft with great masts or long stakes, bound tight with hemp ropes and bamboo cables, joined into a pontoon ark.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Lu devised a method to force the water back into the old channel. On the seventh day of the ninth month—the day guichou—he arrayed twenty-seven large boats against the current, lashed bow to stern with great masts or long stakes using hemp rope and bamboo cable to form a floating barrier.

sentences.zh: 又用大麻索、竹縆用船身繳繞上下，令牢不可破，乃以鐵貓於上流垂之水中。

translations.literal: Hemp ropes and bamboo cables were again wound around the boats above and below, making them so firm they could not be broken; then iron anchors were lowered from upstream into the water.
translations.idiomatic: More hemp rope and bamboo cable were wound around the hulls above and below until the assembly was unbreakable, then iron anchors were dropped from upstream into the water.

sentences.zh: 又以竹縆絕長七八百尺者，系兩岸大橛上，每縆或垂二舟或三舟，使不得下，船腹略鋪散草，滿貯小石，以合子板釘合之，復以掃密布合子板上，或二重，或三重，以大麻索縛之急，復縛橫木三道於頭桅，皆以索維之，用竹編笆，夾以草石，立之桅前，約長丈餘，名曰水簾桅。

translations.literal: Bamboo cables seven or eight hundred chi long were again tied to great stakes on both banks; each cable suspended two or three boats so they could not drift downstream; the boat bellies were lightly spread with loose grass and filled full with small stones, closed with joined boards nailed together; fascines were again densely spread on the joined boards, two or three layers; bound tight with hemp ropes; three cross timbers were again bound to the bow masts, all secured with ropes; bamboo woven fences, packed with grass and stone, were set before the masts, about one zhang or more in length, called water-curtain masts.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo cables seven or eight hundred chi long were tied to great stakes on both banks, each cable holding two or three boats in place against the current. The hulls were lined with loose grass and packed with small stones, then sealed with nailed boards. Fascines were laid on the boards in two or three layers and bound tight with hemp rope. Three crossbeams were lashed to each bow mast. Bamboo mat fences packed with grass and stone, about one zhang long, were set before the masts as water-curtain screens.

sentences.zh: 復以木榰拄，使簾不偃仆，然後選水工便捷者，每船各二人，執斧鑿，立船首尾，岸上搥鼓為號，鼓鳴，一時齊鑿，須臾舟穴，水入，舟沈，遏決河。

translations.literal: Wooden props were again set to brace them, so the curtains would not topple; then nimble water workers were chosen, two for each boat, holding axes and chisels, standing at bow and stern; on the bank drums were beaten as signals; when the drums sounded, all chiseled together; in a moment the boats were holed, water entered, the boats sank, and the breach river was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Wooden braces were set so the water-curtain screens would not collapse. Nimble water workers were chosen—two per boat—with axes and chisels at bow and stern. Drums on the bank signaled the moment; at a single beat all chiseled together. Within moments the hulls were holed, the boats sank, and the breach was sealed.

sentences.zh: 水怒溢，故河水暴增，即重樹水簾，令後復布小掃土牛白闌長梢，雜以草土等物，隨以填垛以繼之。

translations.literal: The water surged angrily and overflowed; the old-channel water swelled greatly; then the water curtains were set up again heavily, ordering that afterward small fascines, earth clods, white fence stones, and long brush be spread again, mixed with grass and earth and other materials, and embankments filled in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The water roared and overflowed, swelling the old channel. Workers rebuilt the water-curtain screens and layered small fascines, earth clods, white limestone, and long brush mixed with grass and earth, filling embankments in succession.

sentences.zh: 石船下詣實地，出水基趾漸高，復卷大掃以壓之。

translations.literal: The stone ships settled to solid ground; as they emerged the foundation base gradually rose higher; great fascines were again rolled to press them down.
translations.idiomatic: As the stone ships settled onto solid ground and their foundations rose above the water, workers rolled great fascines atop them for added weight.

sentences.zh: 前船勢略定，尋用前法，沈余船以竟後功。

translations.literal: Once the leading boats' force was somewhat settled, the former method was soon applied again, sinking the remaining boats to complete the final work.
translations.idiomatic: Once the first boats had stabilized the current, Jia Lu used the same method to sink the rest and finish the closure.

sentences.zh: 昏曉百刻，役夫分番甚勞，無少間斷。

translations.literal: From dusk to dawn through the hundred quarters of the day, laborers in rotating shifts were greatly wearied, without the least interruption.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night through every watch, laborers worked in relays without a moment's pause.

sentences.zh: 船堤之後，草掃三道並舉，中置竹絡盛石，並掃置樁，系纜四掃及絡，一如修北截水堤之法。

translations.literal: After the boat dike, three grass fascine courses were raised together; bamboo cages filled with stone were placed in the middle; stakes were set alongside the fascines; cables bound the four fascines and cages, exactly like the method for repairing the northern river-cutting dike.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the boat dike, three layers of grass fascines were built with stone-filled bamboo cages between them, stakes driven alongside, and cables binding all four fascines and cages—by the same method used on the northern river-cutting dike.

sentences.zh: 第以中流水深數丈，用物之多，施功之大，數倍他堤。

translations.literal: Only because midstream water was several zhang deep, the materials used were many, and the labor applied was great—several times that of other dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Midstream the water ran several zhang deep, requiring far more materials and labor than any other section of dike.

sentences.zh: 船堤距北岸才四五十步，勢迫東河，流峻若自天降，深淺叵測。

translations.literal: The boat dike was only forty or fifty paces from the north bank; the force pressed the eastern river; the current was steep as if descending from heaven; depth and shallowness could not be measured.
translations.idiomatic: The boat dike stood only forty or fifty paces from the north bank, pressed by the eastern current rushing down like a fall from heaven, its depth impossible to gauge.

sentences.zh: 於是先卷下大掃約高二丈者，或四或五，始出水面。

translations.literal: Thereupon great fascines about two zhang high were first rolled down, four or five of them, before they began to emerge above the water surface.
translations.idiomatic: Workers first rolled down great fascines about two zhang high—four or five of them—before any crest broke the surface.

sentences.zh: 修至河口一二十步，用工尤艱。

translations.literal: Repairing to within ten or twenty paces of the river mouth, the labor applied was especially arduous.
translations.idiomatic: The last ten or twenty paces to the river mouth required the most grueling labor of all.

sentences.zh: 薄龍口，喧豗猛疾，勢撼掃基，陷裂欹傾，俄遠故所，觀者股弁，眾議騰沸，以為難合，然勢不容已。

translations.literal: Near the dragon mouth the roar was violent and swift; the force shook the fascine base; it cracked, split, and leaned askew, soon far from its original place; observers' thighs trembled; public discussion seethed, thinking union impossible; yet the force of circumstances would not permit stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Near the dragon mouth the current roared so violently it shook the fascine foundation, cracking and tilting it from its position. Onlookers trembled; many declared the gap could never be closed—yet there was no turning back.

sentences.zh: 魯神色不動，機解捷出，進官吏工徒十餘萬人，日加獎諭，辭旨懇至，眾皆感激赴功。

translations.literal: Lu's expression did not change; his resourceful solutions came forth swiftly; he advanced before more than one hundred thousand officials, clerks, and laborers, daily adding encouragement and rewards; his words were earnest in intent; all were moved with gratitude and rushed to the work.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Lu's composure never wavered. He devised solution after solution and daily exhorted the more than one hundred thousand officials and laborers under his command with such earnest encouragement that all threw themselves gratefully into the work.

sentences.zh: 十一月十一日丁巳，龍口遂合，決河絕流，故道復通。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the eleventh month, the day dingsi, the dragon mouth was then closed; the breach river's flow ceased; the old channel was restored.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day of the eleventh month—the day dingsi—the dragon mouth closed, the breach ceased to flow, and the old channel was open once more.

sentences.zh: 又於堤前通卷欄頭掃各一道，多者或三或四，前掃出水，管心大索系前掃，垂後闌頭掃之後，後掃管心大索亦系小掃，垂前闌頭掃之前，後先羈縻，以錮其勢。

translations.literal: Again before the dike, railing-head fascines were rolled through in one course each, in some cases three or four; the front fascine emerged above water; the great core rope of the front fascine was tied to the front fascine and lowered behind the rear railing-head fascine; the rear fascine's great core rope also tied a small fascine and lowered it before the front railing-head fascine; front and rear were tethered to restrain the force.
translations.idiomatic: Before the dike workers rolled railing-head fascines—one course, sometimes three or four. The forward fascine broke the surface; its core rope was lashed forward and the rear fascine's core rope lashed back, front and rear tethered together to pin the current in place.

sentences.zh: 又於所交索上及兩掃之間，壓以小石白闌土牛，草土相半，厚薄多寡，相勢措置。

translations.literal: Again upon the crossing ropes and between the two fascines, small stones, white fence stones, and earth clods were pressed down, grass and earth in equal parts, thick or thin and more or less placed according to the force of circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: On the crossing ropes and between fascine layers they packed small stones, white limestone, and earth clods mixed with grass and earth, adjusting thickness to the force of the current.

sentences.zh: 掃堤之後，自南岸復修一堤，抵已閉之龍口，長二百七十步。

translations.literal: After the fascine dike, from the south bank a dike was again repaired, reaching the already closed dragon mouth, two hundred seventy paces long.
translations.idiomatic: After the fascine dike, a further dike was built from the south bank to the closed dragon mouth, two hundred seventy paces long.

sentences.zh: 船堤四道成堤，用農家場圃之具曰轆軸者，穴石立木如比櫛，珣前掃之旁，每步置一轆軸，以橫木貫其後，又穴石，以徑二寸余麻索貫之，系橫木上，密掛龍尾大掃，使夏秋潦水、冬春淩筼，不得肆力於岸。

translations.literal: The four boat-dike courses forming a dike used the farm implement for fields and gardens called a windlass; holes were cut in stone and wood set like a comb's teeth, suspending beside the forward fascine; at every pace one windlass was placed, with a cross timber run through behind it; holes were cut in stone again, and hemp rope more than two inches in diameter was run through, tied to the cross timber above, and great dragon-tail fascines densely hung, so that summer and autumn floodwaters and winter and spring ice could not unleash their force upon the bank.
translations.idiomatic: Where the four boat-dike sections formed a continuous embankment, workers used farm windlasses: stone sockets and wooden teeth set like a comb beside each forward fascine, one windlass every pace, crossbeams threaded through, and two-inch hemp rope lashed above to hang great dragon-tail fascines densely, so summer floods and winter ice could not assault the bank.

sentences.zh: 此堤接北岸截河大堤，長二百七十步，南廣百二十步，顛至水面高丈有七尺，水面至澤腹高四丈二尺；

translations.literal: This dike joined the north-bank river-cutting great dike, two hundred seventy paces long; the south face one hundred twenty paces wide; from crest to water surface one zhang and seven chi high; from water surface to the belly of the marsh four zhang and two chi;
translations.idiomatic: This dike connected to the north-bank river-cutting dike, two hundred seventy paces long and one hundred twenty paces wide on the south face—one zhang seven chi from crest to waterline, four zhang two chi from waterline to marsh bottom;

sentences.zh: 中流廣八十步，顛至水面高丈有五尺，水面至澤腹高五丈五尺；

translations.literal: the midstream section eighty paces wide; from crest to water surface one zhang and five chi high; from water surface to the belly of the marsh five zhang and five chi;
translations.idiomatic: the midstream section eighty paces wide stood one zhang five chi above the water and five zhang five chi from waterline to marsh bottom;

sentences.zh: 通高七丈。

translations.literal: total height seven zhang.
translations.idiomatic: seven zhang in total height.

sentences.zh: 仍治南岸護堤掃一道，通長百三十步，南岸護岸馬頭掃三道，通長九十五步。

translations.literal: The south-bank protective dike fascine was still treated, one course totaling one hundred thirty paces in length; south-bank bank-protecting horse-head fascines three courses, totaling ninety-five paces in length.
translations.idiomatic: Workers also built a south-bank protective fascine one hundred thirty paces long and three horse-head fascines along the south bank totaling ninety-five paces.

sentences.zh: 修築北岸堤防，高廣不等，通長二百五十四里七十一步。

translations.literal: North-bank dikes were repaired and built, with height and width unequal, totaling two hundred fifty-four li and seventy-one paces in length.
translations.idiomatic: North-bank dikes were repaired and built along two hundred fifty-four li and seventy-one paces, varying in height and width.

sentences.zh: 白茅河口至板城，補築舊堤，長二十五里二百八十五步。

translations.literal: From Baimao River mouth to Bancheng, old dikes were patched, twenty-five li and two hundred eighty-five paces long.
translations.idiomatic: From the Baimao river mouth to Bancheng, old dikes were patched for twenty-five li and two hundred eighty-five paces.

sentences.zh: 曹州板城至英賢村等處，高廣不等，長一百三十三里二百步。

translations.literal: From Bancheng in Caozhou to Yingxian Village and other places, with height and width unequal, one hundred thirty-three li and two hundred paces long.
translations.idiomatic: From Caozhou's Bancheng to Yingxian Village and beyond, dikes of varying dimensions extended one hundred thirty-three li and two hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 梢岡至碭山縣，增培舊堤，長八十五里二十步。

translations.literal: From Shaogang to Dangshan County, old dikes were heightened and banked, eighty-five li and twenty paces long.
translations.idiomatic: From Shaogang to Dangshan County, existing dikes were raised and strengthened for eighty-five li and twenty paces.

sentences.zh: 歸德府哈只口至徐州路三百餘里，修完缺口一百七處，高廣不等，積修計三里二百五十六步。

translations.literal: From Hazhi Mouth in Guide Prefecture to Xuzhou Circuit, more than three hundred li; one hundred seven breach gaps were fully repaired, with height and width unequal, accumulated repair totaling three li and two hundred fifty-six paces.
translations.idiomatic: From Guide Prefecture's Hazhi Mouth to Xuzhou Circuit—over three hundred li—one hundred seven breach gaps were closed, the cumulative new work totaling three li and two hundred fifty-six paces.

sentences.zh: 亦思剌店縷水月堤，高廣不等，長六里三十步。

translations.literal: The thread-water moon dike at Yisila Shop, with height and width unequal, six li and thirty paces long.
translations.idiomatic: A thread-water moon dike at Yisila Shop ran six li and thirty paces, varying in height and width.

sentences.zh: 其用物之凡，樁木大者二萬七千，榆柳雜梢六十六萬六千，帶梢連根株者三千六百，槁稭蒲葦雜草以束計者七百三十三萬五千有奇，竹竿六十二萬五千，葦席十有七萬二千，小石二千艘，繩索小大不等五萬七千，所沈大船百有二十，鐵纜三十有二，鐵貓三百三十有四，竹篾以斤計者十有五萬，垂石三千塊，鐵鉆萬四千二百有奇，大釘三萬三千二百三十有二。

translations.literal: The materials used in total: large piles twenty-seven thousand; elm and willow mixed brush six hundred sixty-six thousand; with branches and roots attached three thousand six hundred; straw, reed, and mixed grass in bundles seven million three hundred thirty-five thousand and a fraction; bamboo poles six hundred twenty-five thousand; reed mats one hundred seventy-two thousand; small stones two thousand boatloads; ropes large and small fifty-seven thousand; large boats sunk one hundred twenty; iron cables thirty-two; iron anchors three hundred thirty-four; bamboo splints in jin fifteen thousand; suspended stones three thousand blocks; iron drills fourteen thousand two hundred and a fraction; large nails thirty-three thousand two hundred thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Materials consumed in total: twenty-seven thousand large piles; six hundred sixty-six thousand bundles of elm and willow brush; three thousand six hundred with roots attached; seven million three hundred thirty-five thousand bundles of straw, reed, and grass; six hundred twenty-five thousand bamboo poles; one hundred seventy-two thousand reed mats; two thousand boatloads of small stone; fifty-seven thousand ropes of all sizes; one hundred twenty large boats sunk; thirty-two iron cables; three hundred thirty-four iron anchors; fifteen thousand jin of bamboo splints; three thousand suspended stone blocks; fourteen thousand two hundred iron drills; thirty-three thousand two hundred thirty-two large nails.

sentences.zh: 其餘若木龍、蠶椽木、麥稭、扶樁、鐵叉、鐵吊、枝麻、搭火鉤、汲水、貯水等具皆有成數。

translations.literal: The rest, such as wooden dragons, silkworm-rafter wood, wheat straw, support stakes, iron forks, iron hoists, branch hemp, fire-hook frames, water-drawing, water-storage, and other implements all had fixed counts.
translations.idiomatic: Every other implement—wooden dragons, silkworm-rafter timber, wheat straw, support stakes, iron forks, hoists, branch hemp, fire-hooks, water-drawing and storage gear—was accounted for in fixed quantities.

sentences.zh: 官吏俸給，軍民衣糧工錢，醫藥、祭祀、賑恤、驛置馬乘及運竹木、沈船、渡船、下樁等工，鐵、石、竹、木、繩索等匠傭貲，兼以和買民地為河，並應用雜物等價，通計中統鈔百八十四萬五千六百三十六錠有奇。

translations.literal: Official salaries, military and civilian clothing, grain, and labor wages, medicine, sacrifices, relief, relay stations' horses and transport, and labor for hauling bamboo and timber, sinking boats, ferry boats, driving piles, and craftsmen's wages for iron, stone, bamboo, wood, and rope, together with compensated purchase of civilian land for the river and prices of miscellaneous supplies needed, totaled in all one million eight hundred forty-five thousand six hundred thirty-six ding and a fraction of Zhongtong paper notes.
translations.idiomatic: Official salaries, soldiers' and civilians' provisions and wages, medicine, sacrifices, relief, relay transport, hauling timber, sinking boats, ferries, pile-driving, and wages for ironworkers, stonemasons, carpenters, and rope-makers, plus land purchased from civilians for the river and all miscellaneous costs, totaled one million eight hundred forty-five thousand six hundred thirty-six ding and a fraction in Zhongtong paper notes.

sentences.zh: 魯嘗有言：「水工之功，視土工之功為難；

translations.literal: Lu once said: 'The achievement of water work is regarded as harder than earth work;'
translations.idiomatic: Jia Lu once observed: 'Water engineering is harder than earthworks;'

sentences.zh: 中流之功，視河濱之功為難；

translations.literal: 'work in midstream is regarded as harder than work at the riverbank;'
translations.idiomatic: 'midstream work is harder than bank work;'

sentences.zh: 決河口視中流又難；

translations.literal: 'work at the breach mouth is regarded as harder still than midstream;'
translations.idiomatic: 'and work at the breach mouth is harder still than midstream;'

sentences.zh: 北岸之功視南岸為難。

translations.literal: 'work on the north bank is regarded as harder than work on the south bank.'
translations.idiomatic: 'while work on the north bank is harder than on the south.'

sentences.zh: 用物之效，草雖至柔，柔能狎水，水漬之生泥，泥與草並，力重如碇。

translations.literal: 'As for the efficacy of materials, though grass is extremely soft, softness can tame water; when water soaks it, mud is produced; mud together with grass, their force is heavy as a mooring stone.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Among materials, grass is softest, yet softness tames water; soaked in water it becomes mud, and mud mixed with grass weighs like an anchor.'

sentences.zh: 然維持夾輔，纜索之功實多。

translations.literal: 'Yet for maintaining and bracing, the achievement of cables and ropes is truly great.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Yet for holding everything together, ropes and cables do the greater part of the work.'

sentences.zh: 」蓋由魯習知河事，故其功之所就如此。

translations.literal: ' This was because Lu was practiced in river affairs, and so what his achievement accomplished was thus.'
translations.idiomatic: This was the measure of what Jia Lu accomplished—because he truly understood river work.

sentences.zh: 玄之言曰：「是役也，朝廷不惜重費，不吝高爵，為民辟害。

translations.literal: Xuan's words say: 'This labor— the court did not begrudge heavy expense, did not stint high ranks, to open harm away from the people.'
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xuan wrote: 'In this project the court spared no expense and granted the highest honors, all to spare the people from flood disaster.'

sentences.zh: 脫脫能體上意，不憚焦勞，不恤浮議，為國拯民。

translations.literal: 'Toghto was able to embody the ruler's intent, not fearing exhausting toil, not heeding floating criticism, to save the state and rescue the people.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Toghto embodied the emperor's will, heedless of exhaustion and public criticism, to save the realm and its people.'

sentences.zh: 魯能竭其心思智計之巧，乘其精神膽氣之壯，不惜劬瘁，不畏譏評，以報君相知人之明。

translations.literal: 'Lu was able to exhaust the ingenuity of his mind and cleverness in planning, ride the vigor of his spirit and courage, not sparing strenuous labor, not fearing ridicule and criticism, to repay the ruler's knowledge of men.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Jia Lu poured out every resource of mind and courage, shrank from no toil and no ridicule, to repay the emperor's trust in recognizing talent.'

sentences.zh: 宜悉書之，使職史氏者有所考證也。」

translations.literal: 'It is fitting that all be written in full, so that those charged with the historical record may have material for verification.'
translations.idiomatic: 'All of this should be recorded fully, that future historians may have evidence to consult.'

sentences.zh: 先是歲庚寅，河南北童謠云：「石人一隻眼，挑動黃河天下反。

translations.literal: Earlier in the year gengyin, north and south of the Yellow River a children's rhyme said: "A stone man with one eye, stirring the Yellow River, the realm will rebel."
translations.idiomatic: In the gengyin year a children's rhyme ran through the Yellow River region: 'A stone man with one eye—stir the Yellow River and the realm will rise in revolt.'

sentences.zh: 」及魯治河，果於黃陵岡得石人一眼，而汝、潁之妖寇乘時而起。

translations.literal: ' When Lu controlled the river, indeed at Huangling Hillock a stone man with one eye was obtained, while demonic bandits in Ru and Ying rose up seizing the moment.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Lu undertook the river project, workers indeed unearthed a one-eyed stone figure at Huangling Hillock, even as rebel armies rose in the Ru and Ying regions.

sentences.zh: 議者往往以謂天下之亂，皆由賈魯治河之役，勞民動眾之所致。

translations.literal: Discussants often said that the realm's disorder was all caused by Jia Lu's river-control labor, through exhausting the people and mobilizing the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Critics often blamed the fall of the dynasty on Jia Lu's river project, claiming that mobilizing the masses had brought down the state.

sentences.zh: 殊不知元之所以亡者，實基於上下因循，狃於宴安之習，紀綱廢弛，風俗偷薄，其致亂之階，非一朝一夕之故，所由來久矣。

translations.literal: They did not know that the reason the Yuan perished was in fact rooted in upper and lower levels' routine acquiescence, addiction to habits of ease and security, statutes and discipline relaxed, customs decadent and thin—the stages leading to disorder were not the work of a morning or evening, but had long been developing.
translations.idiomatic: They failed to see that the Yuan's collapse had far deeper roots: decades of complacency at court, lax discipline, and moral decay—the path to chaos had been long in the making.

sentences.zh: 不此之察，乃獨歸咎於是役，是徒以成敗論事，非通論也。

translations.literal: Not examining this, yet solely blaming this labor—this is merely judging affairs by success or failure, not a comprehensive view.
translations.idiomatic: To ignore all that and blame this project alone is to judge by success or failure, not by reason.

sentences.zh: 設使賈魯不興是役，天下之亂，詎無從而起乎？

translations.literal: Suppose Jia Lu had not undertaken this labor—would the realm's disorder have had no occasion to arise?
translations.idiomatic: Had Jia Lu never undertaken the project, would rebellion not have erupted anyway?

sentences.zh: 今故具錄玄所記，庶來者得以詳焉。

translations.literal: Now therefore Xuan's record is set forth in full, so that those to come may obtain detail.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore record Ouyang Xuan's account in full, that posterity may understand the project in detail.

sentences.zh: ○蜀堰

translations.literal: ○ Shu Irrigation Works
translations.idiomatic: ○ Shu Irrigation Works

sentences.zh: 江水出蜀西南僥外，東至於岷山，而禹導之。

translations.literal: The Yangtze River emerges from the remote southwest of Shu, flows east to Mount Min, and Yu channeled it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze rises in the far southwest of Shu, flows east to Mount Min, and Yu the Great channeled it there.

sentences.zh: 秦昭王時，蜀太守李冰鑿離堆，分其江以灌川蜀，民用以饒。

translations.literal: In the time of King Zhaoxiang of Qin, Shu governor Li Bing cut through the Li Heap, divided the river to irrigate the Shu plain, and the people grew prosperous thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Zhaoxiang of Qin, Shu governor Li Bing cut the Li Heap, split the river to irrigate the Chengdu Plain, and the people prospered.

sentences.zh: 歷千數百年，所過沖薄蕩嚙，又大為民患。

translations.literal: Over a thousand years, where it passed it was scoured, thinned, washed, and gnawed away, and again became a great affliction for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Over the centuries the current scoured and undercut its banks until the river again became a grave affliction.

sentences.zh: 有司以故事，歲治堤防，凡一百三十有三所，役兵民多者萬餘人，少者千人，其下猶數百人。

translations.literal: The authorities followed precedent, annually repairing dikes, in all one hundred thirty-three places; conscripted soldiers and civilians numbered at most more than ten thousand, at least one thousand, and below that still several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: By custom officials repaired dikes at one hundred thirty-three locations each year, drafting up to ten thousand soldiers and civilians, or as few as several hundred.

sentences.zh: 役凡七十日，不及七十日，雖事治，不得休息。

translations.literal: Labor lasted seventy days in all; if less than seventy days, even when the work was done, rest was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée lasted seventy days; even after work was finished, laborers could not rest until the full term was served.

sentences.zh: 不役者，日出三緡為庸錢。

translations.literal: Those not conscripted paid three strings per day as substitute money.
translations.idiomatic: Those not drafted paid three strings of cash per day in lieu of labor.

sentences.zh: 由是富者屈於貲，貧者屈於力，上下交病，會其費，歲不下七萬緡。

translations.literal: Thus the rich were bent by expense, the poor bent by labor; upper and lower alike suffered; gathering the costs, each year no less than seventy thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: The rich were crushed by fees, the poor by labor; everyone suffered alike. Annual costs ran to at least seventy thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 大抵出於民者，十九藏於吏，而利之所及，不足以償其費矣。

translations.literal: Generally what came from the people, nineteen parts were hoarded by clerks, and the benefit that reached them was insufficient to repay the expense.
translations.idiomatic: Of what the people paid, nineteen parts in twenty lined officials' pockets, while the benefit they received scarcely repaid the cost.

sentences.zh: 元統二年，僉四川肅政廉訪司事吉當普巡行周視，得要害之處三十有二，余悉罷之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuantong, Jidangpu, associate commissioner of the Sichuan Surveillance and Investigation Office, made a circuit inspection and identified thirty-two key locations; the rest were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuantong 2 Jidangpu of the Sichuan surveillance commission toured the works, identified thirty-two critical sites, and abolished the rest.

sentences.zh: 召灌州判官張弘，計曰：「若甃之以石，則歲役可罷，民力可蘇矣。

translations.literal: He summoned Guanzhou assistant magistrate Zhang Hong and planned, saying: 'If we face them with stone, then annual corvée can be abolished and the people's strength can be restored.'
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Guanzhou assistant magistrate Zhang Hong and said: 'If we rebuild the works in stone, annual corvée can end and the people can recover.'

sentences.zh: 」弘曰：「公慮及此，生民之福，國家之幸，萬世之利也。

translations.literal: Hong said: 'The lord has considered this— it is the people's blessing, the state's good fortune, and benefit for ten thousand generations.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong replied: 'Your foresight is the people's blessing, the state's fortune, and a benefit for ten thousand generations.'

sentences.zh: 」弘遂出私錢，試為小堰，堰成，水暴漲而堰不動。

translations.literal: Hong then contributed private funds, testing with a small weir; when the weir was completed, water rose violently but the weir did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong spent his own funds to build a trial weir; when floodwaters surged, the structure held firm.

sentences.zh: 乃具文書，會行省及蒙古軍七翼之長、郡縣守宰，下及鄉里之老，各陳利害，咸以為便。

translations.literal: Documents were then prepared, meeting with the provincial administration and the commanders of seven Mongol garrison wings, prefectural and county magistrates, down to village elders, each stating advantages and disadvantages; all regarded it as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted formal proposals and convened provincial officials, commanders of seven Mongol garrison wings, magistrates, and village elders; all agreed the plan was sound.

sentences.zh: 復禱於冰祠，卜之吉。

translations.literal: Prayer was again offered at the Bing shrine; divination was auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: They prayed at Li Bing's shrine and received an auspicious divination.

sentences.zh: 於是征工發徒，以仍改至元元年十有一月朔日，肇事於都江堰，即禹鑿之處，分水之源也。

translations.literal: Thereupon laborers were conscripted and workers mobilized; on the first day of the eleventh month of the first year after the change to Zhiyuan, work began at Dujiangyan—that place Yu cut through, the source of dividing the waters.
translations.idiomatic: Labor was then mobilized. On the first day of the eleventh month of Zhiyuan 1 work began at Dujiangyan—the place Yu cut the river, source of the water division.

sentences.zh: 鹽井關限其西北，水西關據其西南，江南北皆東行。

translations.literal: Yanjing Pass bounded it to the northwest; Shuixi Pass held its southwest; north and south of the river all flowed east.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjing Pass lay to the northwest, Shuixi Pass to the southwest; both branches of the divided river ran east.

sentences.zh: 北舊無江，冰鑿以辟沫水之害，中為都江堰，少東為大、小釣魚，又東跨二江為石門，以節北江之水，又東為利民臺，臺之東南為侍郎、楊柳二堰，其水自離堆分流入於南江。

translations.literal: To the north there had originally been no river; Bing cut through to avert the harm of the Mo River; in the middle was Dujiangyan; slightly east were Great and Small Diaoyu; further east spanning the two rivers was Stone Gate, to regulate the north river's water; further east was Limin Terrace; southeast of the terrace were the Shilang and Yangliu weirs; their water from the Li Heap divided and flowed into the south river.
translations.idiomatic: Northward there had been no channel until Bing cut one to divert the Mo River. Dujiangyan stood at the center; slightly east were Great and Small Diaoyu; farther east Stone Gate spanned both rivers to regulate the north branch; farther east Limin Terrace, southeast of which lay the Shilang and Yangliu weirs, whose waters from the Li Heap fed the south river.

sentences.zh: 南江東至鹿角，又東至金馬口，又東道大安橋，入於成都，俗稱大皂江，江之正源也。

translations.literal: The south river flowed east to Lujiao, then east to Jinma Mouth, then east past Da'an Bridge into Chengdu; commonly called Great Zaojiang River—it was the river's main source.
translations.idiomatic: The south river ran east to Lujiao, then to Jinma Mouth, then past Da'an Bridge into Chengdu—the Great Zaojiang, main stream of the system.

sentences.zh: 北江少東為虎頭山，為鬥雞臺。

translations.literal: The north river flowed slightly east to Tiger Head Mountain, which was Cockfight Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The north river ran slightly east to Tiger Head Mountain—the Cockfight Terrace.

sentences.zh: 臺有水則，以尺畫之，凡十有一。

translations.literal: On the terrace was a water gauge marked in chi; in all there were eleven.
translations.idiomatic: The terrace bore a water gauge marked in eleven chi gradations.

sentences.zh: 水及其九，其民喜，過則憂，沒其則則困。

translations.literal: When water reached the ninth mark the people rejoiced; if it passed that they worried; if it submerged the gauge they were distressed.
translations.idiomatic: When the water reached the ninth mark the people rejoiced; above it they grew anxious; at flood level they despaired.

sentences.zh: 又書「深淘灘，高作堰」六字其旁，為治水之法，皆冰所為也。

translations.literal: Also inscribed beside it were the six characters 'Deeply dredge the shoals, build the weir high'—the method of controlling water, all done by Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Beside it Bing had inscribed six characters: 'Deeply dredge the shoals, build the weir high'—his fundamental rule for water control.

sentences.zh: 又東為離堆，又東過淩虛、步雲二橋，又東至三石洞，釃為二渠。

translations.literal: Further east was the Li Heap; further east passing Lingxu and Buyun bridges; further east to Three Stone Cave, where it was divided into two channels.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east lay the Li Heap, then the Lingxu and Buyun bridges, then Three Stone Cave where the river split in two.

sentences.zh: 其一自上馬騎東流，過郫，入於成都，古謂之內江，今府江是也；

translations.literal: One from Shangmaqi flowed east, passed Pi, and entered Chengdu—anciently called the Inner River, today's Fu River;
