translations.idiomatic: One branch ran east from Shangmaqi through Pi into Chengdu—the ancient Inner River, today's Fu River;

sentences.zh: 其一自三石洞北流，過將軍橋，又北過四石洞，折而東流，過新繁，入於成都，古謂之外江。

translations.literal: one from Three Stone Cave flowed north, passed General Bridge, again north past Four Stone Cave, then turned east, passed Xinfan, and entered Chengdu—anciently called the Outer River.
translations.idiomatic: the other flowed north from Three Stone Cave past General Bridge and Four Stone Cave, then turned east through Xinfan into Chengdu—the ancient Outer River.

sentences.zh: 此冰所穿二江也。

translations.literal: These were the two rivers Bing cut through.
translations.idiomatic: These were the two channels Li Bing had cut.

sentences.zh: 南江自利民臺有支流，東南出萬工堰，又東為駱駝，又東為碓口，繞青城而東，鹿角之北涯，有渠曰馬壩，東流至成都，入於南江。

translations.literal: From Limin Terrace the south river had a branch flowing southeast out through Wangong Weir, then east as Luotuo, then east as Duikou, winding east around Qingcheng; on the north bank of Lujiao was a channel called Maba, flowing east to Chengdu and entering the south river.
translations.idiomatic: From Limin Terrace a branch ran southeast through Wangong Weir, east as Luotuo, then Duikou, circling Qingcheng. North of Lujiao the Maba channel ran east to Chengdu and rejoined the south river.

sentences.zh: 渠東行二十餘里，水決其南涯四十有九，每歲疲民力以塞之。

translations.literal: The channel flowed east more than twenty li; water breached its south bank in forty-nine places; every year the people's strength was exhausted to block them.
translations.idiomatic: That channel ran eastward over twenty li, its south bank breached in forty-nine places—every year exhausting the people to plug the breaks.

sentences.zh: 乃自其北涯鑿二渠，與楊柳渠合，東行數十里，復與馬壩渠會，而渠成安流。

translations.literal: Thereupon from its north bank two channels were cut, joining the Yangliu channel, flowing east several tens of li, again meeting the Maba channel, and the channel then flowed peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: Workers cut two channels from the north bank into the Yangliu channel, running east several tens of li to rejoin Maba, and the whole system ran smoothly.

sentences.zh: 自金馬口之西鑿二渠，合金馬渠，東南入於新津江，罷藍澱、黃水、千金、白水、新興至三利十二堰。

translations.literal: West of Jinma Mouth two channels were cut, joining the Jinma channel, flowing southeast into the Xinjin River, abolishing the twelve weirs from Landian through Huangshui, Qianjin, Baishui, and Xinxing to Sanli.
translations.idiomatic: West of Jinma Mouth two more channels were cut into the Jinma channel and southeast to the Xinjin River, eliminating twelve weirs from Landian, Huangshui, Qianjin, Baishui, Xinxing through Sanli.

sentences.zh: 北江三石洞之東為外應、顏上、五斗諸堰，外應、顏上之水皆東北流，入於外江。

translations.literal: East of Three Stone Cave on the north river were the Waiying, Yanshang, and Wudou weirs; Waiying and Yanshang waters all flowed northeast into the outer river.
translations.idiomatic: East of Three Stone Cave on the north river lay the Waiying, Yanshang, and Wudou weirs; Waiying and Yanshang waters ran northeast into the outer river.

sentences.zh: 五斗之水，南入馬壩渠，皆內江之支流也。

translations.literal: Wudou water flowed south into the Maba channel—all branches of the inner river.
translations.idiomatic: Wudou water ran south into Maba channel—all inner-river branches.

sentences.zh: 外江東至崇寧，亦為萬工堰。

translations.literal: The outer river flowed east to Chongning, also forming Wangong Weir.
translations.idiomatic: The outer river ran east to Chongning, where it too formed Wangong Weir.

sentences.zh: 堰之支流，自北而東，為三十六洞，過清白堰東入於彭、漢之間。

translations.literal: The weir's branch channels from north to east were thirty-six openings, passing east of Qingbai Weir into the region between Peng and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Branch channels ran north and east in thirty-six openings, passing east of Qingbai Weir into the Peng-Han basin.

sentences.zh: 而清白堰水潰其南涯，延袤三里餘，有司因潰以為堰。

translations.literal: But Qingbai Weir water breached its south bank, extending more than three li; the authorities made the breach into a weir.
translations.idiomatic: Qingbai Weir's south bank had breached for over three li; officials had tried to turn the breach itself into a weir.

sentences.zh: 堰輒壞，乃疏其北涯舊渠，直流而東，罷其堰及三十六洞之役。

translations.literal: The weir repeatedly failed; thereupon the old channel on its north bank was dredged to flow straight east, abolishing that weir and the labor on the thirty-six openings.
translations.idiomatic: The weir kept failing, so workers dredged the old north-bank channel straight east, abandoning the weir and the thirty-six openings.

sentences.zh: 嘉定之青神，有堰曰鴻化，則授成其長吏，應期而功畢。

translations.literal: At Qingshen in Jiading was a weir called Honghua; its magistrate was entrusted to complete it, and the work finished on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingshen in Jiading the Honghua Weir was entrusted to the local magistrate, who finished on schedule.

sentences.zh: 若成都之九里堤，崇寧之萬工堰，彰之堋口、豐潤、千江、石洞、濟民、羅江、馬腳諸堰，工未及施，則召長吏勉諭，使及農隙為之。

translations.literal: As for Chengdu's Nine-li Dike, Chongning's Wangong Weir, Zhang's Bengkou, Fengrun, Qianjiang, Shidong, Jimin, Luojiang, Majiao and other weirs—where work had not yet been applied, magistrates were summoned and urged to complete them in the agricultural off-season.
translations.idiomatic: For Chengdu's Nine-li Dike, Chongning's Wangong Weir, and weirs at Bengkou, Fengrun, Qianjiang, Shidong, Jimin, Luojiang, Majiao and elsewhere not yet started, magistrates were urged to finish during the farming slack season.

sentences.zh: 諸堰都江及利民臺之役最大，侍郎、楊柳、外應、顏上、五斗次之，鹿角、萬工、駱駝、碓口、三利又次之。

translations.literal: Among the weirs, Dujiangyan and Limin Terrace labor was greatest; Shilang, Yangliu, Waiying, Yanshang, and Wudou came next; Lujiao, Wangong, Luotuo, Duikou, and Sanli came after that.
translations.idiomatic: The greatest works were Dujiangyan and Limin Terrace; next Shilang, Yangliu, Waiying, Yanshang, and Wudou; then Lujiao, Wangong, Luotuo, Duikou, and Sanli.

sentences.zh: 而都江又居大江中流，故以鐵萬六千斤，鑄為大龜，貫以鐵柱，而鎮其源，然後即工。

translations.literal: And because Dujiangyan again lay in midstream of the great river, therefore sixteen thousand jin of iron was cast into a great turtle, pierced with an iron pillar, to anchor the source, and only then was work undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: Because Dujiangyan sits in midstream, sixteen thousand jin of iron was cast into a great turtle anchored with an iron pillar at the source before construction began.

sentences.zh: 諸堰皆甃以石，範鐵以關其中，取桐實之油，和石灰，雜麻絲，而搗之使熟，以苴罅漏。

translations.literal: All weirs were faced with stone; iron frames were set within; tung-seed oil was taken, mixed with lime and hemp fiber, pounded until cooked, to plug cracks and leaks.
translations.idiomatic: Every weir was stone-faced with iron frames inside, sealed with a mortar of tung oil, lime, and pounded hemp fiber.

sentences.zh: 岸善崩者，密築江石以護之，上植楊柳，旁種蔓荊，櫛比鱗次，賴以為固，蓋以數百萬計。

translations.literal: Where banks readily collapsed, river stones were densely piled for protection; willows were planted above, creeping vines beside, scale-like in rows depending on them for solidity—in all numbering in the millions.
translations.idiomatic: Banks prone to collapse were armored with river stone, topped with willows and creeping vines planted in dense rows—millions of plantings in all.

sentences.zh: 所至或疏舊渠以導其流，或鑿新渠以殺其勢。

translations.literal: Where they arrived, sometimes old channels were dredged to guide the flow, sometimes new channels cut to reduce the force.
translations.idiomatic: Old channels were dredged to guide flow where needed; new channels cut to reduce destructive force.

sentences.zh: 遇水之會，則為石門，以時啟閉而泄蓄之，用以節民力而資民利，凡智力所及，無不為也。

translations.literal: Where waters met, stone gates were made, opened and closed according to season to discharge and store, used to economize the people's labor and enrich the people's benefit; whatever intelligence could reach, nothing was left undone.
translations.idiomatic: At confluences stone gates were built, opened and closed seasonally to store or release water, sparing labor and enriching the people—nothing within human power was left undone.

sentences.zh: 初，郡縣及兵家共掌都江之政，延祐七年，其兵官奏請獨任郡縣，民不堪其役‖至是復合焉。

translations.literal: Initially prefectures, counties, and military units jointly administered Dujiangyan affairs; in the seventh year of Yanyou the military officer memorialized requesting sole charge by prefectures and counties—the people could not bear the labor ‖ at this time it was again combined.
translations.idiomatic: Originally civil and military authorities jointly managed Dujiangyan; in Yanyou 7 the military petitioned for sole county control, which oppressed the people—now authority was reunified.

sentences.zh: 常歲獲水之利僅數月，堰輒壞，至是，雖緣渠所置碓硙紡績之處以千萬計，四時流轉而無窮。

translations.literal: In normal years the benefit of water lasted only a few months and the weir repeatedly failed; at this time, though places along the channels for pestles, mills, and spinning numbered in the tens of millions, they turned through the four seasons without end.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly irrigation lasted only months before weirs failed; now mills and workshops along the channels numbered in the millions, running year-round without cease.

sentences.zh: 其始至都江，水深廣莫可測，忽有大洲湧出其西南，方可數里，人得用事其間。

translations.literal: When work first reached Dujiangyan, the water's depth and breadth could not be measured; suddenly a great sandbar emerged to the southwest, about several li square, and people could work upon it.
translations.idiomatic: When work began at Dujiangyan the depth was immeasurable—then a great sandbar emerged to the southwest, several li across, giving workers dry ground.

sentences.zh: 入山伐石，崩石已滿，隨取而足。

translations.literal: Entering the mountains to quarry stone, fallen stone already filled the area; taking as needed was sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Quarrying in the mountains, fallen stone lay everywhere in abundance.

sentences.zh: 蜀故多雨，自初役至工畢，無雨雪，故力省而功倍，若有相之者。

translations.literal: Shu is accustomed to much rain; from the first labor until work was completed there was no rain or snow; therefore strength was saved and achievement doubled, as if something assisted.
translations.idiomatic: Shu is rainy country, yet from start to finish of the project no rain or snow fell—labor was halved and progress doubled, as if heaven assisted.

sentences.zh: 五越月，功告成，而吉當普以監察御史召，省臺上其功，詔揭扌奚斯制文立碑以旌之。

translations.literal: In five months work was announced complete; Jidangpu was summoned as surveillance censor; the provincial offices reported his achievement; an edict ordered Jie'ansi to compose text and erect a stele to honor it.
translations.idiomatic: In five months the work was done. Jidangpu was recalled as censor; the provincial administration reported his merit; the court ordered Jie'ansi to compose an inscription and erect a commemorative stele.

sentences.zh: 是役也，凡石工、金工皆七百人，木工二百五十人，役徒三千九百人，而蒙古軍居其二千。

translations.literal: This labor: stone workers and metalworkers seven hundred each, woodworkers two hundred fifty, laborers three thousand nine hundred, of whom Mongol soldiers were two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The workforce comprised seven hundred stonemasons, seven hundred metalworkers, two hundred fifty carpenters, and three thousand nine hundred laborers—two thousand of them Mongol soldiers.

sentences.zh: 糧為石千有奇，石之材取於山者百萬有奇，石之灰以斤計者六萬有奇，油半之，鐵六萬五千斤，麻五千斤。

translations.literal: Grain for stone more than a thousand and a fraction; stone timber taken from the mountains more than a million and a fraction; stone lime in jin more than sixty thousand and a fraction; oil half that amount; iron sixty-five thousand jin; hemp five thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: Grain for the stonework exceeded one thousand shi; mountain stone exceeded one million units; lime sixty thousand jin; oil half that quantity; iron sixty-five thousand jin; hemp five thousand jin.

sentences.zh: 撮其工之直、物之價，以緡計者四萬九千有奇，皆出於民之庸，而在官之積者，尚余二十萬一千八百緡，責灌守以貸於民，歲取其息，以備祭祀及淘灘修堰之費。

translations.literal: Gathering the straight value of labor and the price of materials, reckoned in strings, forty-nine thousand and a fraction—all came from the people's corvée; yet what accumulated in government stores still remained two hundred one thousand eight hundred strings; the Guanzhou prefect was charged to lend it to the people, annually taking interest, to prepare for sacrifices and the expenses of dredging shoals and repairing weirs.
translations.idiomatic: Labor and materials cost forty-nine thousand strings, all from corvée levies on the people. Government stores still held two hundred one thousand eight hundred strings, which the Guanzhou prefect was ordered to lend out at interest to fund sacrifices and annual dredging and repairs.

sentences.zh: 仍蠲灌之兵民所常徭役，俾專其力於堰事。

translations.literal: Still exempting Guanzhou's soldiers and civilians from their usual corvée, so they could devote their strength solely to weir affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Regular corvée on soldiers and civilians in Guanzhou was also waived so they could devote all their strength to the weirs.

sentences.zh: ○涇渠

translations.literal: ○ Jing Canal
translations.idiomatic: ○ Jing Canal

sentences.zh: 涇渠者，在秦時韓使水工鄭國說秦，鑿涇水，自仲山西抵瓠口為渠，並北山，東註於洛三百餘里以溉田，蓋欲以罷秦之力，使無東伐。

translations.literal: The Jing Canal: in Qin times Han sent the water engineer Zheng Guo to persuade Qin; he cut the Jing River from Zhongshan west to Hugu Mouth as a canal, along the northern mountains, east pouring into the Luo for more than three hundred li to irrigate fields—intending thereby to exhaust Qin's strength so it would not attack east.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing Canal: in Qin times the state of Han sent the engineer Zheng Guo to persuade Qin to cut a channel from the Jing River at Zhongshan west to Hugu Mouth, running three hundred li east along the northern foothills into the Luo to irrigate farmland—intending to exhaust Qin's strength and forestall eastern campaigns.

sentences.zh: 秦覺其謀，欲殺之，鄭曰：「臣為韓延數年之命，而為秦建萬世之利。

translations.literal: Qin perceived his scheme and wished to kill him; Zheng said: 'I have extended Han's life by several years, yet built ten thousand generations' benefit for Qin.'
translations.idiomatic: When Qin uncovered the plot and moved to execute him, Zheng Guo said: 'I have bought Han a few more years of life, yet built benefit for Qin that will last ten thousand generations.'

sentences.zh: 」秦以為然，使迄成之，號鄭渠。

translations.literal: Qin regarded this as correct and had him complete it to the end; it was named the Zheng Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Qin accepted this argument and let him finish the work, naming it the Zheng Canal.

sentences.zh: 漢時有白公者，奏穿渠引涇水，起谷口，入櫟陽，註渭中，袤二百里，溉田四千五百餘頃，因名曰白渠。

translations.literal: In Han times there was one called Lord Bai, who memorialized to cut a canal drawing Jing water, starting from Gukou, entering Liyang, pouring into the Wei, more than two hundred li in extent, irrigating fields four thousand five hundred and more qing; it was therefore named the Bai Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Lord Bai memorialized for a canal drawing Jing water from Gukou through Liyang into the Wei—over two hundred li irrigating more than four thousand five hundred qing—hence the Bai Canal.

sentences.zh: 歷代因之，皆享其利。

translations.literal: Through successive dynasties they followed it, all enjoying its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Successive dynasties maintained it and all reaped its benefits.

sentences.zh: 至宋時，水沖嚙，失其故跡。

translations.literal: By Song times, water scoured and gnawed away, and the old traces were lost.
translations.idiomatic: By the Song period scouring had erased the old course.

sentences.zh: 熙寧間，詔賜常平息錢，助民興作，自仲山旁開鑿石渠，從高瀉水，名豐利渠。

translations.literal: During the Xining period, an edict granted Ever-Normal Granary interest money to assist the people in construction; from beside Zhongshan a stone channel was opened, discharging water from high ground, named the Fengli Canal.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining reign the court granted Ever-Normal Granary interest funds to help civilians rebuild; a stone aqueduct was cut beside Zhongshan to carry water from higher ground—the Fengli Canal.

sentences.zh: 元至元間，立屯田府督治之。

translations.literal: In the Zhiyuan period of Yuan, a garrison-farmland office was established to supervise its governance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuan Zhiyuan a garrison-farmland office was established to oversee the works.

sentences.zh: 大統八年，涇水暴漲，毀堰塞渠，陜西行省命屯田府總管夾谷伯顏帖木兒及涇陽尹王琚疏道之，起涇陽、高陵、三原、櫟陽用水人戶及渭南、櫟陽、涇陽三屯所人夫，共三千餘人興作，水通流如舊。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dadu, the Jing River rose violently, destroying the weir and blocking the canal; the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat ordered the garrison-farmland office director Jiagu Boyan Timur and Jingyang magistrate Wang Ju to dredge the channel; from Jingyang, Gaoling, Sanyuan, and Liyang water-user households and the laborers of three garrison farms at Weinan, Liyang, and Jingyang, more than three thousand in all, were mobilized for construction; water flowed as of old.
translations.idiomatic: In Dadu 8 the Jing River flooded, destroying the weir and blocking the canal. The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat ordered garrison-farmland director Jiagu Boyan Timur and Jingyang magistrate Wang Ju to dredge it, mobilizing more than three thousand water-user households and garrison laborers from Jingyang, Gaoling, Sanyuan, Liyang, Weinan, and elsewhere until flow was restored.

sentences.zh: 其制編荊為囤，貯之以石，復填以草以土為堰，歲時葺理，未嘗廢止。

translations.literal: The method was to weave thorns into bins, store stone in them, again fill with grass and earth to make a weir; seasonally repaired and maintained, never abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Thorn bins were woven, filled with stone, then packed with grass and earth to form a weir—maintained seasonally without interruption.

sentences.zh: ○金口河

translations.literal: ○ Jinkou River
translations.idiomatic: ○ Jinkou River

sentences.zh: 至正二年正月，中書參議孛羅帖木兒、都水傅佐建言，起自通州南高麗莊，直至西山石峽鐵板開水古金口一百二十餘里，創開新河一道，深五丈，廣二十丈，放西山金口水東流至高麗莊，合御河，接引海運至大都城內輸納。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Zhizheng, Central Secretariat counselor Boluotiemuer and Director of Waterworks Fu Zuo proposed starting from Gaolizhuang south of Tongzhou straight to the ancient Jinkou at the Stone Gorge Iron Plate west of the mountains, more than one hundred twenty li, to open a new river course, five zhang deep and twenty zhang wide, releasing western-mountain Jinkou water to flow east to Gaolizhuang, joining the Imperial Canal, drawing sea transport into the capital for delivery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhizheng 2 counselor Boluotiemuer and Director of Waterworks Fu Zuo proposed opening a new channel from Gaolizhuang south of Tongzhou to the ancient Jinkou at Stone Gorge Iron Plate west of the mountains—over one hundred twenty li, five zhang deep and twenty zhang wide—to divert western mountain water east to Gaolizhuang, join the Imperial Canal, and bring sea transport into the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時，脫脫為中書右丞相，以其言奏而行之。

translations.literal: At this time Toghto was Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat and memorialized their words to put them into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Toghto, then Right Chancellor, endorsed the proposal and ordered it carried out.

sentences.zh: 廷臣多言其不可，而左丞許有壬言尤力，脫脫排群議不納，務於必行。

translations.literal: Court ministers mostly said it could not be done, and Left Chancellor Xu Youren spoke especially forcefully; Toghto overrode the crowd of opinions and would not accept them, insisting it must be done.
translations.idiomatic: Most court ministers opposed the plan; Left Chancellor Xu Youren argued most forcefully. Toghto overrode all dissent and insisted on proceeding.

sentences.zh: 有壬因條陳其利害，略曰：

translations.literal: Youren therefore set forth its advantages and harms in items, saying in summary:
translations.idiomatic: Xu Youren then submitted a detailed memorandum on the project's risks, in summary stating:

sentences.zh: 大德二年，渾河水發為民害，大都路都水監將金口下閉閘板。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade, the Hun River rose and harmed the people; the Dadu Circuit Directorate of Waterworks closed the sluice boards below Jinkou.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 2 the Hun River flooded and harmed the people; the Dadu waterworks directorate closed the sluice boards below Jinkou.

sentences.zh: 五年間，渾河水勢浩大，郭太史恐沖沒田薛二村、南北二城，又將金口已上河身，用砂石雜土盡行堵閉。

translations.literal: Within five years the Hun River's force was vast; Guo Shoujing feared it would wash away the Tian and Xue villages and the northern and southern cities; again the river body above Jinkou was entirely blocked with mixed sand, stone, and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Within five years the Hun grew so powerful that Guo Shoujing feared it would wash away the Tian and Xue villages and both city walls; the channel above Jinkou was then entirely sealed with sand, stone, and earth.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，因行都水監郭道壽言，金口引水過京城至通州，其利無窮，工部官並河道提舉司、大都路及合屬官員耆老等相視議擬，水由二城中間窒礙。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun, on the words of metropolitan waterworks director Guo Daoshou that drawing Jinkou water through the capital to Tongzhou would bring boundless benefit, Ministry of Works officials together with the river-course intendant, Dadu Circuit, and subordinate officials and elders inspected and deliberated; the water was obstructed passing between the two cities.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 1 metropolitan waterworks director Guo Daoshou claimed that drawing Jinkou water through the capital to Tongzhou would yield boundless benefit. After inspection by Ministry of Works officials, the river intendant, Dadu Circuit, and local elders, they found the water blocked between the two city walls.

sentences.zh: 又盧溝河自橋至合流處，自來未嘗有漁舟上下，此乃不可行船之明驗也。

translations.literal: Moreover, from the Lugou Bridge to the confluence, fishing boats had never gone up or down—this was clear proof that boats could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, from Lugou Bridge to the confluence fishing boats had never navigated the reach—clear proof the route was unnavigable.

sentences.zh: 且通州去京城四十里，盧溝止二十里，此時若可行船，當時何不於盧溝立馬頭，百事近便，卻於四十里外通州為之？

translations.literal: And Tongzhou is forty li from the capital, Lugou only twenty li; if boats could pass then, why not build wharves at Lugou, where everything was nearer and convenient, yet instead do it at Tongzhou forty li away?
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou lies forty li from the capital, Lugou only twenty. If shipping had been feasible, why build wharves at distant Tongzhou rather than convenient Lugou?

sentences.zh: 又西山水勢高峻，亡金時，在都城之北流入郊野，縱有沖決，為害亦輕。

translations.literal: Moreover, western-mountain water force is high and steep; in the defunct Jin period it flowed into the suburbs north of the capital, and even if it breached, the harm was light.
translations.idiomatic: Western mountain water runs high and steep. Under the defunct Jin it entered the suburbs north of the capital; even when it breached, damage was limited.

sentences.zh: 今則在都城西南，與昔不同。

translations.literal: Now it would be southwest of the capital, unlike the past.
translations.idiomatic: Now the channel would lie southwest of the capital—a wholly different situation.

sentences.zh: 此水性本湍急，若加以夏秋霖潦漲溢，則不敢必其無虞，宗廟社稷之所在，豈容僥幸於萬一？

translations.literal: This water by nature is already swift; if summer and autumn rains and floods are added, one dare not be certain there would be no mishap; the place where the ancestral temples and altars of state stand—how can one gamble on a one-in-ten-thousand chance?
translations.idiomatic: The current is swift by nature; add summer and autumn floods and disaster is likely. How can one gamble with the ancestral temples and state altars?

sentences.zh: 若一時成功，亦不能保其永無沖決之患。

translations.literal: If it succeeded for a time, still it could not be guaranteed there would never be breach disaster thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Even temporary success could not guarantee against future breaches.

sentences.zh: 且亡金時此河未必通行，今所有河道遺跡，安知非作而復輟之地乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, in Jin times this river may not necessarily have been navigable; today's surviving traces of the channel—who knows whether they are places where work was begun and then abandoned?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Jin canal may never have been navigable; existing traces may mark projects begun and abandoned.

sentences.zh: 又地形高下不同，若不作閘，必致走水淺澀，若作閘以節之，則沙泥渾濁，必致淤塞，每年每月專人挑洗，蓋無窮盡之時也。

translations.literal: Also terrain high and low differs; if no sluice is built, water will certainly run off shallow and sluggish; if sluices are built to regulate it, sand and mud will be turbid and certainly cause silting; every year every month specialists will dredge—there would be no end to it.
translations.idiomatic: Terrain varies in elevation: without sluices water runs shallow; with sluices turbid silt blocks the channel, requiring endless monthly dredging.

sentences.zh: 且郭太史初作通惠河時，何不用此水，而遠取白浮之水，引入都城，以供閘壩之用？

translations.literal: Moreover, when Guo Shoujing first made the Tonghui Canal, why did he not use this water but draw from afar the Baiteng waters into the capital to supply sluice and dam use?
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Shoujing built the Tonghui Canal, why did he draw clear Baiteng water from afar rather than this turbid source?

sentences.zh: 蓋白浮之水澄清，而此水渾濁不可用也。

translations.literal: Because Baiteng water is clear, while this water is turbid and cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: Because Baiteng water is clear and this water is too turbid for sluice use.

sentences.zh: 此議方興，傳聞於外，萬口一辭，以為不可。

translations.literal: As this deliberation arose, rumor spread outside; ten thousand mouths with one voice said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: As debate spread, public opinion united overwhelmingly against the project.

sentences.zh: 若以為成大功者不謀於眾，人言不足聽，則是商鞅、王安石之法，當今不宜有此。

translations.literal: If one thinks that those who accomplish great works do not consult the multitude and people's words need not be heard, then that is the law of Shang Yang and Wang Anshi—such should not exist in the present age.
translations.idiomatic: To claim great works need not heed public opinion is the logic of Shang Yang and Wang Anshi—unsuited to our age.

sentences.zh: 議既上，丞相終不從，遂以正月興工，至四月功畢。

translations.literal: Once the memorial was submitted, the chancellor ultimately would not follow it; yet work began in the first month and was completed in the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xu Youren's memorial was ignored, work began in the first month and was declared finished by the fourth.

sentences.zh: 起閘放金口水，流湍勢急，沙泥壅塞，船不可行，而開挑之際，毀民廬舍墳塋，夫丁死傷甚眾，又費用不貲，卒以無功。

translations.literal: Sluices were opened to release Jinkou water; the current was swift and forceful, sand and mud silted it, and boats could not pass; during the opening and dredging, civilian houses and graves were destroyed, laborers died and were injured in great numbers, expense was beyond reckoning, and in the end it came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When the sluices opened, the torrent silted up immediately; boats could not pass. Excavation destroyed homes and graves; many laborers died. Costs were incalculable—and the project failed utterly.

sentences.zh: 繼而御史糾劾建言者，孛羅帖木兒、傅佐俱伏誅。

translations.literal: Thereafter censors impeached the proposers; Boluotiemuer and Fu Zuo were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: Censors then impeached the proposers; Boluotiemuer and Fu Zuo were both executed.

sentences.zh: 今附載其事於此，用為妄言水利者之戒。

translations.literal: Now this affair is appended here in full, to serve as a warning for those who speak rashly of water control.
translations.idiomatic: Their story is recorded here as a warning to those who speak rashly of water projects.
